# EliteReads

> Curated reading lists from Elon Musk, Bill Gates, and 100+ top leaders. Every book recommendation sourced and verified.

## Main Pages

- [Home](https://elitereads.com): Discover curated book recommendations from the world's top leaders and thinkers
- [Explore](https://elitereads.com/explore): Browse all elites, books, genres, and topics
- [Most Recommended](https://elitereads.com/most-recommended): Books recommended by the most elites
- [Top Picks](https://elitereads.com/top-picks): Editor-curated standout book recommendations
- [Insights](https://elitereads.com/insights): Articles and insights about reading and leadership

## Elites

### [Tim Ferriss](https://elitereads.com/elite/tim-ferriss) — Author of The 4-Hour Workweek & Podcaster

Tim Ferriss is an early-stage technology investor (Uber, Facebook, Shopify) and the author of five #1 New York Times and Wall Street Journal bestsellers, including The 4-Hour Workweek and Tools of Titans. He is the host of The Tim Ferriss Show podcast, which has exceeded 900 million downloads and is often called "the Oprah of audio" for its influence on book sales and lifestyle trends.

**Recommended books:**
- [Vagabonding](https://elitereads.com/book/vagabonding) by Rolf Potts — "Vagabonding easily remains in my top-10 list of life-changing books. Why? Because one incredible trip, especially a long-term trip, can change your life forever."
- [The Magic of Thinking Big](https://elitereads.com/book/the-magic-of-thinking-big) by David J. Schwartz — "This book is about thinking big in terms of the scope of your ambition... It is one of the books I have gifted the most."
- [The Effective Executive](https://elitereads.com/book/the-effective-executive-peter-drucker) by Peter F. Drucker — "I think it's much more valuable than 99% of the so-called time management books out there. It is the one book to read on effectiveness."
- [Letters from a Stoic](https://elitereads.com/book/letters-from-a-stoic) by Lucius Annaeus Seneca — "My favorite book of all time. I've read it dozens of times."
- [Radical Acceptance](https://elitereads.com/book/radical-acceptance) by Tara Brach — "It ended up exceeding all my expectations – it really had a profound impact on my life."
- [Dune](https://elitereads.com/book/dune-frank-herbert) by Frank Herbert — "All you need to know about leadership is contained in Dune."
- [Awareness](https://elitereads.com/book/awareness-anthony-de-mello) by Anthony de Mello — "It's good medicine for the right people at the right time. I keep a full shelf of this book in my guest bedroom."
- [Gold](https://elitereads.com/book/gold-rumi) by Rumi — "Outstanding collection... very easy to read, not intended to be read front to back. It's like a little night cap before you go to sleep."
- [The E-Myth Revisited](https://elitereads.com/book/the-e-myth-revisited) by Michael E. Gerber — "Why most small businesses don't work and what to do about it. This is a classic."
- [How to Make Millions with Your Ideas](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-make-millions-with-your-ideas) by Dan S. Kennedy — "This book is a menu of options for converting ideas into cash."
- [The 80/20 Principle](https://elitereads.com/book/the-80-20-principle) by Richard Koch — "This book changed my life and is the basis for The 4-Hour Workweek."
- [Poor Charlie's Almanack](https://elitereads.com/book/poor-charlies-almanack) by Charles T. Munger — "One of the wisest people you can learn from... This book is timeless."
- [The Obstacle Is the Way](https://elitereads.com/book/the-obstacle-is-the-way) by Ryan Holiday — "A very good entry point into Stoicism for modern readers."
- [Little, Big](https://elitereads.com/book/little-big-john-crowley) by John Crowley — "Little, Big is simply one of the best novels I've ever read, and even that doesn't do it justice. It is mysteriously affecting."
- [Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind](https://elitereads.com/book/sapiens-a-brief-history-of-humankind) by Yuval Noah Harari — "I recently read Sapiens and it's phenomenal."
- [Zorba the Greek](https://elitereads.com/book/zorba-the-greek) by Nikos Kazantzakis — "One of my favorite fiction books. It teaches you to love the questions themselves."
- [The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse](https://elitereads.com/book/the-boy-the-mole-the-fox-and-the-horse) by Charlie Mackesy — "This short and beautiful book was gifted to me by my mom. It looks like a children's book... but it's replete with wisdom for adults."
- [Stranger in a Strange Land](https://elitereads.com/book/stranger-in-a-strange-land) by Robert A. Heinlein — "A mind-bending classic."
- [Musashi](https://elitereads.com/book/musashi) by Eiji Yoshikawa — "The 'Gone with the Wind' of Japan. A long epic about the greatest swordsman in Japanese history."
- [The Checklist Manifesto](https://elitereads.com/book/the-checklist-manifesto) by Atul Gawande — "Ramit and I are both obsessed with checklists and love this book."
- [Bird by Bird](https://elitereads.com/book/bird-by-bird-anne-lamott) by Anne Lamott — "A superb book on writing and life."
- [On Writing Well](https://elitereads.com/book/on-writing-well) by William Zinsser — "The classic guide to writing non-fiction."
- [The 22 Immutable Laws of Marketing](https://elitereads.com/book/the-22-immutable-laws-of-marketing) by Al Ries, Jack Trout — "I've read this book multiple times."
- [How to Change Your Mind](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-change-your-mind) by Michael Pollan — "A very, very good primer for people who want an overview [of psychedelics] and the science."
- [Don't Shoot the Dog!](https://elitereads.com/book/dont-shoot-the-dog) by Karen Pryor — "The bible of training... whether it's dogs, dolphins, or your spouse."
- [The Name of the Wind](https://elitereads.com/book/the-name-of-the-wind) by Patrick Rothfuss — "I have loved... The Name of the Wind."
- [Anything You Want](https://elitereads.com/book/anything-you-want) by Derek Sivers — "Derek is one of my favorite humans... this book is pure gold."
- [Creativity, Inc.](https://elitereads.com/book/creativity-inc-ed-catmull) by Ed Catmull, Amy Wallace — "No matter your circumstances, storytelling and creativity are two 'meta-skills' that can take your business and life to the next level. Ed is a master."
- [Extreme Ownership](https://elitereads.com/book/extreme-ownership) by Jocko Willink, Leif Babin — "I loved it."
- [Bad Science](https://elitereads.com/book/bad-science) by Ben Goldacre — "A must-read for anyone who wants to understand how we are misled by bad studies."
- [Venture Deals](https://elitereads.com/book/venture-deals) by Brad Feld, Jason Mendelson — "For the fellow tech nerds among you, here are a few resources for learning about angel investing."
- [Reckless](https://elitereads.com/book/reckless-ed-brubaker) by Ed Brubaker, Sean Phillips — "Comic book series I'm loving."
- [Siddhartha](https://elitereads.com/book/siddhartha) by Hermann Hesse — "I think about it often."
- [Man's Search for Meaning](https://elitereads.com/book/mans-search-for-meaning) by Viktor E. Frankl — "This book pops up a ton from my guests... I have read it multiple times."
- [The Sommelier's Atlas of Taste](https://elitereads.com/book/the-sommeliers-atlas-of-taste) by Rajat Parr, Jordan Mackay — "A definitive reference book."
- [Exhalation](https://elitereads.com/book/exhalation) by Ted Chiang — "I have loved... anything by Ted Chiang."

### [Warren Buffett](https://elitereads.com/elite/warren-buffett) — Chairman & CEO of Berkshire Hathaway

Warren Buffett is the Chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway and one of the most successful investors in history. Known as the "Oracle of Omaha," he adheres to a value investing philosophy pioneered by Benjamin Graham. He has pledged to give away 99 percent of his fortune to philanthropic causes, primarily via the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

**Recommended books:**
- [The Intelligent Investor](https://elitereads.com/book/the-intelligent-investor) by Benjamin Graham — "I learned most of the thoughts in this investment discussion from Ben's book The Intelligent Investor, which I bought in 1949. My financial life changed with that purchase... Picking up that book was one of the luckiest moments in my life."
- [Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits](https://elitereads.com/book/common-stocks-and-uncommon-profits) by Philip Fisher — "I am an eager reader of whatever Phil has to say, and I recommend him to you."
- [Business Adventures](https://elitereads.com/book/business-adventures-twelve-classic-tales-from-the-world-of-wall-street) by John Brooks — "Business Adventures remains the best business book I've ever read."
- [The Outsiders](https://elitereads.com/book/the-outsiders-william-thorndike) by William N. Thorndike — "The Outsiders... is an outstanding book about CEOs who excelled at capital allocation. It has an insightful chapter on our director, Tom Murphy, overall the best business manager I've ever met."
- [Stress Test](https://elitereads.com/book/stress-test-reflections-on-financial-crises) by Timothy F. Geithner — "This is a book that every manager should read... It's a must-read for any manager."
- [The Little Book of Common Sense Investing](https://elitereads.com/book/the-little-book-of-common-sense-investing) by John C. Bogle — "Rather than listen to their siren songs, investors – large and small – should instead read Jack Bogle's The Little Book of Common Sense Investing."
- [Where Are the Customers' Yachts?](https://elitereads.com/book/where-are-the-customers-yachts) by Fred Schwed Jr. — "The funniest book ever written about investing, it lightly delivers many truly important messages on the subject."
- [Essays in Persuasion](https://elitereads.com/book/essays-in-persuasion) by John Maynard Keynes — "Reading Keynes will make you smarter about securities and markets. I'm not sure reading most economists would do the same."
- [Shoe Dog](https://elitereads.com/book/shoe-dog) by Phil Knight — "The best book I read last year. Phil is a very wise, intelligent and competitive fellow who is also a gifted storyteller."
- [Jack: Straight from the Gut](https://elitereads.com/book/jack-straight-from-the-gut) by Jack Welch, John A. Byrne — "Get a copy!"
- [Dream Big](https://elitereads.com/book/dream-big-cristiane-correa) by Cristiane Correa — "My friend – and now partner – Jorge Paulo and his team are among the best businessmen in the world. He is a fantastic person and his story should be an inspiration to everybody, as it is for me."
- [First a Dream](https://elitereads.com/book/first-a-dream) by Jim Clayton, Bill Retherford — "I enjoyed the book so much that I gave copies to Pierce, Wolf, my family and the directors of Berkshire."
- [Take on the Street](https://elitereads.com/book/take-on-the-street) by Arthur Levitt — "Levitt's excellent book, Take on the Street."
- [Nuclear Terrorism](https://elitereads.com/book/nuclear-terrorism) by Graham Allison — "A must-read for those concerned with the safety of our country."
- [Bull!: A History of the Boom and Bust, 1982-2004](https://elitereads.com/book/bull-a-history-of-the-boom-and-bust-1982-2004) by Maggie Mahar — "A 2003 book that investors can learn much from is Bull! by Maggie Mahar."
- [The Smartest Guys in the Room](https://elitereads.com/book/the-smartest-guys-in-the-room) by Bethany McLean, Peter Elkind — "Two other books I'd recommend are The Smartest Guys in the Room... and In an Uncertain World."
- [In an Uncertain World](https://elitereads.com/book/in-an-uncertain-world) by Robert E. Rubin, Jacob Weisberg — "Well-reported and well-written."
- [Warren Buffett's Ground Rules](https://elitereads.com/book/warren-buffetts-ground-rules) by Jeremy C. Miller — "Mr. Miller has done a superb job of researching and dissecting the operation of Buffett Partnership Ltd."
- [Limping on Water](https://elitereads.com/book/limping-on-water) by Phil Beuth — "An autobiography that chronicles his life at Capital Cities Communications... tells you a lot about its leaders, Tom Murphy and Dan Burke."
- [A Few Lessons for Investors and Managers](https://elitereads.com/book/a-few-lessons-for-investors-and-managers) by Peter Bevelin — "I think you'll also like a short book that Peter Bevelin has put together explaining Berkshire's investment and operating principles."
- [Tap Dancing to Work](https://elitereads.com/book/tap-dancing-to-work) by Carol J. Loomis — "She has been invaluable to me in editing this letter since 1977."
- [How to Win Friends and Influence People](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-win-friends-and-influence-people) by Dale Carnegie — "It changed my life."
- [The Moment of Lift](https://elitereads.com/book/the-moment-of-lift) by Melinda French Gates — "I think this is one of the best books I've ever read."
- [The Making of the President 1960](https://elitereads.com/book/the-making-of-the-president-1960) by Theodore H. White — "The Making of the President 1960 is as timely today as it was when first published."
- [Personal History](https://elitereads.com/book/personal-history) by Katharine Graham — "Warren viewed Personal History as a seminal episode because it defined her in the public's mind."
- [The Essays of Warren Buffett: Lessons for Corporate America](https://elitereads.com/book/the-essays-of-warren-buffett-lessons-for-corporate-america) by Warren Buffett, Lawrence A. Cunningham — "Larry Cunningham... has produced a definitive statement... New and experienced readers alike will gain an invaluable informal education by perusing this classic arrangement."
- [The Great Crash 1929](https://elitereads.com/book/the-great-crash-1929) by John Kenneth Galbraith

### [Charlie Munger](https://elitereads.com/elite/charlie-munger) — Vice Chairman of Berkshire Hathaway

Charles T. Munger (1924–2023) was the Vice Chairman of Berkshire Hathaway and Warren Buffett’s closest partner for nearly 50 years. A Harvard-educated lawyer who founded the law firm Munger, Tolles & Olson, he is revered for his multidisciplinary approach to investing, famously coining the concept of a 'latticework of mental models.' His sharp wit and wisdom on life, business, and psychology have made him an intellectual icon well beyond the finance world.

**Recommended books:**
- [Guns, Germs, and Steel](https://elitereads.com/book/guns-germs-and-steel) by Jared Diamond — "I have recently read a new book twice, which I very seldom do... It's a marvelous book... I would say it's the best work of its kind I have ever read."
- [The Selfish Gene](https://elitereads.com/book/the-selfish-gene) by Richard Dawkins — "If you take Dawkins, The Selfish Gene and The Blind Watchmaker, I mean, these are marvelous books... I had to read The Selfish Gene twice before I fully understood it."
- [Titan: The Life of John D. Rockefeller, Sr.](https://elitereads.com/book/titan-the-life-of-john-d-rockefeller-sr) by Ron Chernow — "That's one of the best business biographies I have ever read. And it's a very interesting family story, too. That is was just a wonderful, wonderful book."
- [The Outsiders](https://elitereads.com/book/the-outsiders-william-thorndike) by William N. Thorndike — "A book that details the extraordinary success of CEOs who took a radically different approach to corporate management."
- [Ice Age](https://elitereads.com/book/ice-age-john-gribbin-mary-gribbin) by John Gribbin, Mary Gribbin — "I think it's the best book of scientific explanation I have ever read... I recommend that book to you."
- [The Wealth and Poverty of Nations: Why Some Are So Rich and Some So Poor](https://elitereads.com/book/the-wealth-and-poverty-of-nations) by David S. Landes — "It was a wonderful book... I would heartily recommend [this] book."
- [Living within Limits](https://elitereads.com/book/living-within-limits-garrett-hardin) by Garrett Hardin — "Recommended in Poor Charlie's Almanack."
- [The Blind Watchmaker](https://elitereads.com/book/the-blind-watchmaker) by Richard Dawkins — "These are powerful books. And they're a lot of fun... marvelous books."
- [The Third Chimpanzee](https://elitereads.com/book/the-third-chimpanzee) by Jared Diamond — "Recommended in Poor Charlie's Almanack."
- [Genome: The Autobiography of a Species in 23 Chapters](https://elitereads.com/book/genome-the-autobiography-of-a-species-in-23-chapters) by Matt Ridley — "It is a fabulous book... I'm recommending a bestseller."
- [Models of My Life](https://elitereads.com/book/models-of-my-life) by Herbert A. Simon — "An autobiography of Nobel laureate Herbert A. Simon, a remarkable polymath who more people should know about... it's a very interesting book."
- [How the Scots Invented the Modern World](https://elitereads.com/book/how-the-scots-invented-the-modern-world) by Arthur Herman — "It was a marvelous book... I recommend [it] to all of you."
- [The Warren Buffett Portfolio](https://elitereads.com/book/the-warren-buffett-portfolio-robert-g-hagstrom) by Robert G. Hagstrom — "I was flabbergasted to find it not only very well written, but a considerable contribution to the synthesis of human thought on the investment process."
- [A Matter of Degrees: What Temperature Reveals about the Past and Future of Our Species, Planet, and Universe](https://elitereads.com/book/a-matter-of-degrees-gino-segre) by Gino Segrè — "A wide-ranging exploration of how the fundamental scientific concept of temperature is bound up with the very essence of both life and matter."
- [Master of the Game](https://elitereads.com/book/master-of-the-game-connie-bruck) by Connie Bruck — "I very much enjoyed Connie Bruck's biography Master of the Game... she's a very insightful writer and it's a very interesting story."
- [Yes!](https://elitereads.com/book/yes-50-scientifically-proven-ways-to-be-persuasive) by Noah J. Goldstein, Steve J. Martin, Robert B. Cialdini — "He's just got a new book... called Yes! So here's two books that I suggest you add to your class."

- [Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In](https://elitereads.com/book/getting-to-yes) by Roger Fisher, William Ury, Bruce Patton — "Recommended in Poor Charlie's Almanack."

- [Three Scientists and Their Gods: Looking for Meaning in an Age of Information](https://elitereads.com/book/three-scientists-and-their-gods) by Robert Wright — "Recommended in Poor Charlie's Almanack."

### [Peter Thiel](https://elitereads.com/elite/peter-thiel) — Co-founder of PayPal, Palantir & Founders Fund

Peter Thiel is a serial entrepreneur and venture capitalist who co-founded PayPal and Palantir Technologies. He was the first outside investor in Facebook and leads the Founders Fund, having backed companies like SpaceX and Airbnb. A prominent contrarian thinker, he authored the bestselling business book *Zero to One*.

**Recommended books:**
- [Things Hidden Since the Foundation of the World](https://elitereads.com/book/things-hidden-since-the-foundation-of-the-world) by René Girard, Jean-Michel Oughourlian, Guy Lefort — "He’s the one writer who has influenced me the most. ... I think the magisterial one is probably Things Hidden Since the Foundation of the World."
- [Chaos: Charles Manson, the CIA, and the Secret History of the Sixties](https://elitereads.com/book/chaos-charles-manson-the-cia-and-the-secret-history-of-the-sixties) by Tom O'Neill, Dan Piepenbring — "A fantastic book... shows you what they were trying to do to demonize these hippies."
- [The Sovereign Individual](https://elitereads.com/book/the-sovereign-individual) by James Dale Davidson, William Rees-Mogg — "One of the books that tremendously influenced me when I started PayPal."
- [The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test](https://elitereads.com/book/the-electric-kool-aid-acid-test) by Tom Wolfe — "I still think his greatest novel was the Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test, which is sort of this history of the LSD counterculture movement."
- [The Lord of the Rings](https://elitereads.com/book/the-lord-of-the-rings) by J.R.R. Tolkien — "The classic favorite novel I always give is Lord of the Rings. I read it when I was a kid... I still think it's the best."
- [JFK and the Unspeakable](https://elitereads.com/book/jfk-and-the-unspeakable) by James W. Douglass — "Lee Harvey Oswald had obvious connections to U.S. intelligence... In JFK and the Unspeakable, James Douglass argues that President John F. Kennedy was assassinated due to his opposition to the deep state."
- [The Diamond Age: Or, a Young Lady's Illustrated Primer](https://elitereads.com/book/the-diamond-age) by Neal Stephenson — "I started reading this once and was mesmerized by Stephenson’s imaginative future world."
- [The Devil's Chessboard](https://elitereads.com/book/the-devils-chessboard) by David Talbot — "The Warren Commission was headed by Allen Dulles, one of JFK's enemies... [Discussed in context of the deep state and CIA history]"
- [The Hard Thing About Hard Things](https://elitereads.com/book/the-hard-thing-about-hard-things) by Ben Horowitz — "Ben Horowitz knows no recipe guarantees success, and with The Hard Thing About Hard Things, he has written the first true guide for protecting a startup from self-sabotage."
- [Superintelligence](https://elitereads.com/book/superintelligence-nick-bostrom) by Nick Bostrom — "The history of it... was maybe anchored on two visions of what AI meant. And one was Nick Bostrom... [who] wrote this book Superintelligence... AI was going to be this super duper intelligent thing."
- [AI Superpowers: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order](https://elitereads.com/book/ai-superpowers-china-silicon-valley) by Kai-Fu Lee — "The book from Kai-Fu Lee represented the 'CCP rebuttal' to Bostrom's view on the future of AI."
- [Cryptonomicon](https://elitereads.com/book/cryptonomicon) by Neal Stephenson — "The early PayPal team worked well together because we were all the same kind of nerd. We all loved science fiction: Cryptonomicon was required reading."
- [Bloodlands: Europe Between Hitler and Stalin](https://elitereads.com/book/bloodlands-europe-between-hitler-and-stalin) by Timothy Snyder — "Even as he calculates the death toll painstakingly, Mr. Snyder reminds us that the most important number is one: Each victim was an individual whose life cannot be reduced to the violence that cut it short."
- [100 Plus](https://elitereads.com/book/100-plus-sonia-arrison) by Sonia Arrison — "Its message is evergreen: how scientists are directly attacking the problem of aging and death and why we should fight for life instead of accepting decay as inevitable."
- [The Decadent Society](https://elitereads.com/book/the-decadent-society) by Ross Douthat — "Choosing agency over boomer complacency, The Decadent Society sets the stakes for the most urgent public debate of the 2020s: How do we get back to the future?"
- [The Right Stuff](https://elitereads.com/book/the-right-stuff) by Tom Wolfe — "It's both a great history of the space race and a meditation on how to steel yourself to take risks."
- [The Great Illusion](https://elitereads.com/book/the-great-illusion) by Norman Angell — "A tightly reasoned and broadly historical perspective challenging the reigning view that man’s nature is inherently evil."
- [Atlas Shrugged](https://elitereads.com/book/atlas-shrugged) by Ayn Rand — "When I first read them in the late 80s, it still felt pretty crazy, and then the last decade, it’s in many ways felt much more correct."
- [Psychopolitics: Conversations with Trevor Cribben Merrill](https://elitereads.com/book/psychopolitics-jean-michel-oughourlian) by Jean-Michel Oughourlian — "For a fresh application of Mr. Girard's insights into power politics... try Jean-Michel Oughourlian's 'Psychopolitics'."
- [The New Atlantis](https://elitereads.com/book/the-new-atlantis) by Francis Bacon — "Bacon focuses on the duty of the state toward science... [and] anticipate many advances in medicine and surgery."
- [Dangerous](https://elitereads.com/book/dangerous-milo-yiannopoulos) by Milo Yiannopoulos — "If you don't use your freedom of speech, one day you might find that it's gone. Buy this book while it's legal."

### [Steve Jobs](https://elitereads.com/elite/steve-jobs) — Co-founder of Apple & Pixar

Steve Jobs was the co-founder, chairman, and CEO of Apple Inc. and the chairman of Pixar Animation Studios. A pioneer of the personal computer revolution, he oversaw the creation of iconic products including the Macintosh, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, which fundamentally reshaped the technology, music, and film industries. His philosophy of integrating hardware, software, and design defined Apple's global success and legacy.

**Recommended books:**
- [Autobiography of a Yogi](https://elitereads.com/book/autobiography-of-a-yogi) by Paramahansa Yogananda — "Jobs read this book for the first time as a teenager, then rereading it in India and once a year ever since. It was the only book he downloaded to his iPad."

Known for his philosophy of "radical truth" and "radical transparency," he is regarded as one of the most successful investors of all time. ### [Jensen Huang](https://elitereads.com/elite/jensen-huang) — NVIDIA Co-founder & CEO

Jensen Huang is the co-founder and CEO of NVIDIA, serving since its inception in 1993. A visionary in accelerated computing, he pioneered the graphics processing unit (GPU), which transformed the computer graphics industry and ignited the modern AI era. Under his leadership, NVIDIA has grown into the world's most valuable company, powering everything from gaming to autonomous vehicles and scientific computing. ### [Albert Einstein](https://elitereads.com/elite/albert-einstein) — Theoretical Physicist & Nobel Laureate

Albert Einstein was a theoretical physicist widely recognized as one of the greatest and most influential scientists of all time. He developed the theory of relativity, which revolutionized the understanding of space, time, and gravity, and made pivotal contributions to quantum mechanics. Awarded the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the photoelectric effect, his intellectual achievements have made his name synonymous with genius.

### [Nikola Tesla](https://elitereads.com/elite/nikola-tesla) — Inventor of the Modern Electrical Age

Nikola Tesla was a Serbian-American inventor and engineer who designed the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system. His breakthrough induction motor and transformer made the universal transmission of electrical power possible, fundamentally changing global industry. A prolific futurist, he pioneered wireless communication, radio technology, and the Tesla coil, envisioning a world of global connectivity long before its time.

**Recommended books:**
- [Faust](https://elitereads.com/book/faust) by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe — "One of these was Goethe's 'Faust.'... As I uttered these inspiring words the idea came like a flash of lightning and in an instant the truth was revealed."

### [Wong Kar Wai](https://elitereads.com/elite/wong-kar-wai) — Cannes-Winning Hong Kong Filmmaker

Wong Kar Wai is a seminal figure in contemporary cinema, celebrated for his lush, atmospheric visuals and poetic explorations of longing, time, and memory. His unique aesthetic, characterized by vibrant colors and non-linear storytelling, has defined the "Hong Kong cool" of the 1990s and influenced filmmakers worldwide. Key works like "In the Mood for Love" and "Chungking Express" remain touchstones of international arthouse cinema.

### [Karl Marx](https://elitereads.com/elite/karl-marx) — Philosopher, Economist & Revolutionary Socialist

Karl Marx was a German philosopher, economist, and revolutionary socialist whose work laid the foundation for modern communism. He is best known for his analysis of history as a series of class struggles and his critique of the capitalist economic system. His seminal works, including The Communist Manifesto and Das Kapital, have profoundly influenced global politics and intellectual thought.

**Recommended books:**

### [Sigmund Freud](https://elitereads.com/elite/sigmund-freud) — Father of Psychoanalysis

Sigmund Freud was an Austrian neurologist and the founder of psychoanalysis, a clinical method for treating psychopathology through dialogue between a patient and a psychoanalyst. He developed therapeutic techniques such as the use of free association and discovered transference, establishing its central role in the analytic process. His analysis of dreams as wish-fulfillments and his formulation of the Oedipus complex have had a lasting impact on psychology and culture.

### [Brian Chesky](https://elitereads.com/elite/brian-chesky) — Co-founder & CEO of Airbnb

### [Phil Knight](https://elitereads.com/elite/phil-knight) — Nike Co-founder & Chairman Emeritus

Phil Knight is the co-founder and Chairman Emeritus of Nike, Inc., having built the company from a handshake partnership into the world's largest athletic apparel brand. ### [BJ Fogg](https://elitereads.com/elite/bj-fogg) — Founder of Stanford Behavior Design Lab

BJ Fogg is a behavioral scientist and the founder of the Behavior Design Lab at Stanford University. He is the originator of the Fogg Behavior Model, which posits that behavior happens when motivation, ability, and a prompt converge. He combines high-level academic research with a passion for education, making quantum mechanics and cosmology understandable to a global audience.

Richard Thaler is a Nobel Prize-winning economist and the Charles R. Walgreen Distinguished Service Professor of Behavioral Science and Economics at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. He is best known for his pioneering work in behavioral economics, challenging the assumption that people act rationally in markets. Thaler is the author of Misbehaving and co-author of the global bestseller Nudge, which introduced the concept of libertarian paternalism to public policy.

### [Daniel Kahneman](https://elitereads.com/elite/daniel-kahneman) — Nobel Laureate & Behavioral Economics Pioneer

Daniel Kahneman was an Israeli-American psychologist and Nobel Laureate known for his work on the psychology of judgment and decision-making. He challenged the assumption of human rationality in economics, introducing concepts like prospect theory and cognitive biases. His research, often conducted with Amos Tversky, established the field of behavioral economics and influenced disciplines ranging from finance to public policy.

### [Ralph Lauren](https://elitereads.com/elite/ralph-lauren) — Founder of Ralph Lauren Corporation

Ralph Lauren is an iconic American fashion designer and business executive best known for founding the Ralph Lauren Corporation. Born Ralph Lifshitz in the Bronx, he launched his career in 1967 with a line of neckties under the Polo label, eventually expanding into a multi-billion dollar global empire encompassing apparel, home furnishings, and fragrances. His aesthetic, characterizing a blend of rugged Americana and preppy sophistication, fundamentally shaped the global perception of American style.

**Recommended books:**

### [Bernard Arnault](https://elitereads.com/elite/bernard-arnault) — Chairman & CEO of LVMH

Bernard Arnault is the Chairman and CEO of LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton, the world's leading luxury products group. He transformed a loose collection of heritage brands into a global empire that includes Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Tiffany & Co., becoming one of the wealthiest individuals in history. Beyond business, he is a major patron of the arts, having established the Fondation Louis Vuitton to promote contemporary artistic creation in Paris. His leadership style combines long-term vision with an uncompromising focus on creativity and quality.

### [François-Henri Pinault](https://elitereads.com/elite/francois-henri-pinault) — Chairman & CEO of Kering

François-Henri Pinault is the Chairman and CEO of Kering, a role he has held since 2005. He orchestrated the group's transformation from a retail conglomerate (PPR) into a global luxury leader housing iconic brands like Gucci, Balenciaga, and Saint Laurent. He serves as President of Groupe Artémis, the family investment holding that controls Christie’s and the Pinault Collection, which manages major contemporary art museums in Venice and Paris. A prominent figure in the art world, he has significantly expanded his family's collection and influence in cultural patronage. He is also a dedicated philanthropist, known for founding the Kering Foundation to combat violence against women.

### [Changpeng Zhao](https://elitereads.com/elite/changpeng-zhao) — Founder of Binance & Giggle Academy

Changpeng Zhao (CZ) is the founder and former CEO of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume. A software developer by training, he previously built high-frequency trading systems for Wall Street before launching Binance in 2017. ### [Nassim Nicholas Taleb](https://elitereads.com/elite/nassim-taleb) — Scholar of Randomness, Risk & Uncertainty

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is a Lebanese-American essayist, scholar, and former options trader known for his work on the problems of randomness, probability, and uncertainty. He is the author of the Incerto, a five-volume philosophical essay that includes The Black Swan and Antifragile. A Distinguished Professor of Risk Engineering at NYU, he advocates for systems that are 'antifragile'—gaining from disorder rather than merely withstanding it.

### [Harold Bloom](https://elitereads.com/elite/harold-bloom) — Sterling Professor of Humanities at Yale

Harold Bloom was an American literary critic and the Sterling Professor of Humanities at Yale University. He authored over 40 books, including *The Anxiety of Influence* and *The Western Canon*, famously defending the aesthetic value of classic literature against modern critical schools. A MacArthur Fellow and member of the American Academy of Arts and Letters, he reshaped the study of poetry and championed the transformational power of deep reading.

### [Noam Chomsky](https://elitereads.com/elite/noam-chomsky) — Father of Modern Linguistics & Social Critic

A laureate professor at the University of Arizona and institute professor emeritus at MIT, he is widely credited with revolutionizing modern linguistics with his theory of generative grammar. As one of the world's most cited scholars, he has authored over 150 books on topics ranging from syntax to war, politics, and mass media. A vocal critic of U.S. foreign policy and neoliberalism, he remains a leading figure in analytic philosophy and cognitive science.

### [Steven Pinker](https://elitereads.com/elite/steven-pinker) — Johnstone Family Professor of Psychology at Harvard

Steven Pinker is the Johnstone Family Professor of Psychology at Harvard University and a leading expert on visual cognition and psycholinguistics. He is the author of numerous influential books, including The Language Instinct, The Better Angels of Our Nature, and Enlightenment Now, which explore the biological basis of language and the historical decline of violence. A two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist and member of the National Academy of Sciences, Pinker advocates for the importance of reason, science, and humanism in solving global challenges.

### [Thomas Jefferson](https://elitereads.com/elite/thomas-jefferson) — 3rd US President & Declaration Author

Thomas Jefferson was a Founding Father, the principal author of the Declaration of Independence, and the third President of the United States. ### [Phil Jackson](https://elitereads.com/elite/phil-jackson) — 11-Time NBA Champion Coach

Phil Jackson is the most successful coach in NBA history, leading the Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Lakers to a combined 11 championships. Known as the "Zen Master," he revolutionized sports leadership by integrating mindfulness, meditation, and Native American philosophy into his coaching to foster selfless team play. ### [Orna Guralnik](https://elitereads.com/elite/orna-guralnik) — Clinical Psychologist & Psychoanalyst

### [Rory Sutherland](https://elitereads.com/elite/rory-sutherland) — Vice Chairman of Ogilvy UK

### [Cormac McCarthy](https://elitereads.com/elite/cormac-mccarthy) — Pulitzer Prize-Winning American Novelist

Cormac McCarthy was an American novelist and playwright widely regarded as one of the greatest writers of his time. Known for his spare punctuation and dark, existential themes, he chronicled the violence and moral complexity of the American frontier in masterpieces like Blood Meridian and The Road. ### [Werner Herzog](https://elitereads.com/elite/werner-herzog) — Legendary Filmmaker & Author

Werner Herzog is a legendary German filmmaker and author known for his unique blend of documentary and fiction, termed "ecstatic truth." ## Books

### [Tribe of Mentors](https://elitereads.com/book/tribe-of-mentors) by Tim Ferriss

A collection of tools, tactics, and habits from over 100 of the world's top performers across diverse fields. The book features profiles of mentors answering key questions about success, failure, and life priorities to provide a roadmap for navigating challenges and achieving results.

### [The 4-Hour Workweek](https://elitereads.com/book/the-4-hour-workweek) by Tim Ferriss

A guide to lifestyle design that challenges the traditional 9-to-5 work paradigm and deferred-life plan. It introduces the DEAL process—Definition, Elimination, Automation, and Liberation—to help readers automate income and achieve location independence. The book provides practical tools for outsourcing, selective ignorance, and creating a business that funds a flexible lifestyle.

### [Tools of Titans](https://elitereads.com/book/tools-of-titans-tim-ferriss) by Tim Ferriss

Distills the routines and tactics of over 200 world-class performers interviewed on The Tim Ferriss Show. The content covers habits, physical performance, and mental frameworks organized into three pillars: Healthy, Wealthy, and Wise.

### [The 4-Hour Chef](https://elitereads.com/book/the-4-hour-chef) by Tim Ferriss

A comprehensive guide to mastering cooking and the art of accelerated learning. Using culinary skills as a framework, the book introduces the DiSSS method to deconstruct and acquire any new skill in record time.

### [The 4-Hour Body](https://elitereads.com/book/the-4-hour-body) by Tim Ferriss

A comprehensive guide to biohacking the human body, detailing methods for rapid fat loss, muscle gain, and physical performance improvement. Based on over a decade of personal experimentation and research, it introduces minimalist protocols like the Slow-Carb Diet. The book advocates for finding the minimum effective dose to achieve significant physiological results with minimal effort.

### [Musashi](https://elitereads.com/book/musashi) by Eiji Yoshikawa

An epic novel detailing the life and spiritual growth of Miyamoto Musashi, Japan's legendary swordsman. Following the Battle of Sekigahara, Musashi embarks on a multi-year quest for mastery, moving beyond mere violence toward enlightenment and the Way of the Sword.

### [The Effective Executive](https://elitereads.com/book/the-effective-executive-peter-drucker) by Peter F. Drucker

A classic management text that argues effectiveness is a discipline that can and must be learned. Drucker outlines five essential practices for executives, including time management, focusing on outward contribution, and mobilizing strengths. It remains a foundational work for understanding the role of the knowledge worker in modern organizations.

### [Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind](https://elitereads.com/book/sapiens-a-brief-history-of-humankind) by Yuval Noah Harari

A survey of human history from the evolution of archaic human species in the Stone Age to the modern 21st century. It examines the Cognitive, Agricultural, and Scientific Revolutions and how they shaped the development of modern society, religion, and capitalism.

### [The Obstacle Is the Way](https://elitereads.com/book/the-obstacle-is-the-way) by Ryan Holiday

Inspired by the ancient Greek philosophy of Stoicism, this book provides a framework for transforming challenges into opportunities. It explores the three core disciplines of perception, action, and will, illustrated through the lives of historical figures who mastered resilience. The work offers a practical guide to maintaining focus and equanimity when faced with adversity.

### [The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse](https://elitereads.com/book/the-boy-the-mole-the-fox-and-the-horse) by Charlie Mackesy

An illustrated fable about a curious boy, a greedy mole, a wary fox, and a wise horse who travel together in the wilderness. Through their conversations, the four unlikely friends explore universal lessons on kindness, vulnerability, and hope. The book features the author's distinctive ink-and-watercolor illustrations and handwritten text.

### [How to Make Millions with Your Ideas](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-make-millions-with-your-ideas) by Dan S. Kennedy

A comprehensive guide for entrepreneurs on transforming innovative concepts into profitable ventures. Dan Kennedy outlines eight high-probability pathways to wealth and provides strategies for market research, strategic planning, and effective marketing. The book includes real-world success stories and a 'Million Dollar Rolodex' of essential business contacts.

### [Extreme Ownership](https://elitereads.com/book/extreme-ownership) by Jocko Willink, Leif Babin

Two Navy SEAL officers provide a leadership guide based on their experiences during the Battle of Ramadi in Iraq. Each chapter presents a combat lesson, describes the corresponding leadership principle, and demonstrates its application in a business or personal context. The book emphasizes taking full responsibility for every aspect of a mission to achieve team success.

### [The Magic of Thinking Big](https://elitereads.com/book/the-magic-of-thinking-big) by David J. Schwartz

A motivational classic that explores the power of mindset and belief in achieving success. David J. Schwartz provides practical strategies for overcoming fear, building confidence, and setting ambitious goals to reach one's full potential. The book emphasizes that the scale of one's success is determined by the size of one's thinking rather than innate talent or intelligence.

### [Man's Search for Meaning](https://elitereads.com/book/mans-search-for-meaning) by Viktor E. Frankl

A psychiatrist's memoir of surviving Nazi concentration camps, where he observed that prisoners with a sense of purpose were more likely to survive. Frankl introduces logotherapy, a therapeutic method focused on identifying a personal 'will to meaning' as the primary human drive. The work serves as a profound meditation on resilience and the search for purpose in the face of suffering.

### [Radical Acceptance](https://elitereads.com/book/radical-acceptance) by Tara Brach

A guide to overcoming the 'trance of unworthiness' through the practice of mindfulness and self-compassion. The book integrates Western psychology with Buddhist teachings to help individuals heal from feelings of deficiency and shame. It includes guided meditations and clinical stories to support emotional freedom and spiritual awakening.

### [Exhalation](https://elitereads.com/book/exhalation) by Ted Chiang

A collection of nine provocative science fiction stories exploring humanity's oldest questions through a scientific and philosophical lens. The tales delve into themes of time travel, artificial intelligence, and free will, ranging from a portal in ancient Baghdad to a scientist's self-dissection in an alien world.

### [Bird by Bird](https://elitereads.com/book/bird-by-bird-anne-lamott) by Anne Lamott

A classic guide to the craft of writing and the challenges of the creative life. Anne Lamott shares personal anecdotes and practical advice on overcoming writer's block, developing characters, and managing the emotional hurdles of being a writer. The book introduces the influential concept of taking massive tasks 'bird by bird' to maintain focus and momentum.

### [Creativity, Inc.](https://elitereads.com/book/creativity-inc-ed-catmull) by Ed Catmull, Amy Wallace

Ed Catmull, co-founder of Pixar Animation Studios, explores the management principles and spiritual core required to build a sustainable creative culture. The book provides an inside look at the meetings and postmortems that produced films like Toy Story and Finding Nemo. It offers practical advice on leadership, candor, and navigating the inevitable risks of innovation.

### [Anything You Want](https://elitereads.com/book/anything-you-want) by Derek Sivers

Derek Sivers shares forty concise lessons learned from starting, growing, and eventually selling his company, CD Baby, for $22 million. The book serves as a philosophical manifesto for entrepreneurs, advocating for customer-centricity and the pursuit of personal happiness over traditional growth metrics. It emphasizes that business owners have the freedom to create their own rules and design their ventures as personal utopias.

### [The Checklist Manifesto](https://elitereads.com/book/the-checklist-manifesto) by Atul Gawande

Atul Gawande explores how the humble checklist can help professionals manage increasing complexity in their work. Drawing on examples from medicine, aviation, and construction, he demonstrates how simple, repeatable steps can prevent fatal errors and improve outcomes across various fields.

### [Dune](https://elitereads.com/book/dune-frank-herbert) by Frank Herbert

Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune follows Paul Atreides as his family accepts stewardship of a world containing the universe's most precious resource, the spice melange. As a complex struggle for control unfolds, Paul must navigate political betrayal and ancient religious prophecy to secure his family's future.

### [How to Change Your Mind](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-change-your-mind) by Michael Pollan

Michael Pollan investigates the medical and scientific revolution surrounding psychedelic drugs like LSD and psilocybin. Combining historical research with personal travelogue, he explores how these substances are being used to treat conditions such as depression and addiction while illuminating the mysteries of human consciousness.

### [The Name of the Wind](https://elitereads.com/book/the-name-of-the-wind) by Patrick Rothfuss

A legendary hero and magician, now living in obscurity as an innkeeper, tells the true story of his life to a traveling scribe. The narrative recounts his childhood in a troupe of performers, his struggle for survival as an orphan, and his education at a prestigious university for magic.

### [Venture Deals](https://elitereads.com/book/venture-deals) by Brad Feld, Jason Mendelson

A comprehensive guide to the venture capital deal process, demystifying term sheets, negotiations, and the motivations of investors. It provides practical insights for entrepreneurs and lawyers on how to navigate startup funding from seed stages through to acquisition.

### [The E-Myth Revisited](https://elitereads.com/book/the-e-myth-revisited) by Michael E. Gerber

Michael Gerber examines the assumption that technical expertise is sufficient for business success, arguing that most small businesses are founded by technicians rather than entrepreneurs. He details the stages of business growth and explains how to apply franchising principles to create consistent, scalable systems.

### [Bad Science](https://elitereads.com/book/bad-science) by Ben Goldacre

The book examines the various ways in which scientific evidence is misused and misinterpreted by the media, politicians, and the pharmaceutical industry. It provides a critical analysis of topics such as homeopathy, nutritional supplement claims, and the placebo effect while teaching readers how to evaluate scientific claims.

### [On Writing Well](https://elitereads.com/book/on-writing-well) by William Zinsser

A guide to the craft of writing nonfiction, focusing on the fundamental principles of clarity, simplicity, and brevity. William Zinsser shares insights on various forms of the genre, including journalism, memoirs, and technical writing, while emphasizing the importance of a writer's unique voice.

### [Awareness](https://elitereads.com/book/awareness-anthony-de-mello) by Anthony de Mello

A grand synthesis of spiritual wisdom that blends Christian spirituality, Buddhist parables, and psychological insight. The book challenges readers to wake up from their habitual patterns and social conditioning to achieve true self-awareness and inner peace.

### [Siddhartha](https://elitereads.com/book/siddhartha) by Hermann Hesse

Siddhartha follows the spiritual journey of a young Brahmin in ancient India who leaves his home to seek enlightenment. After exploring the extremes of asceticism, worldly success, and sensual love, he eventually finds ultimate wisdom through the simple observations of a river and the life of a ferryman.

### [Little, Big](https://elitereads.com/book/little-big-john-crowley) by John Crowley

Smoky Barnable travels to the mysterious estate of Edgewood to marry Daily Alice Drinkwater, only to find himself entangled in a century-spanning family chronicle. As four generations of the Drinkwater family live on the magical border of an otherworld, they navigate a complex 'Tale' that shapes their destinies. The novel blends domestic realism with the ethereal presence of fairies and shifting dimensions.

### [Letters from a Stoic](https://elitereads.com/book/letters-from-a-stoic) by Lucius Annaeus Seneca

A collection of 124 letters written by the Roman statesman and philosopher Seneca to his friend Lucilius. The work serves as a practical guide to Stoic philosophy, providing advice on the pursuit of virtue, the value of friendship, and maintaining mental resilience in the face of death and adversity.

### [Zorba the Greek](https://elitereads.com/book/zorba-the-greek) by Nikos Kazantzakis

A bookish narrator travels to Crete to open a lignite mine and meets the exuberant Alexis Zorba, a man who lives with a primal intensity. Through their singular friendship, the narrator is challenged to abandon his intellectual detachment and embrace the joy and tragedy of life through dance and experience.

### [The Sommelier's Atlas of Taste](https://elitereads.com/book/the-sommeliers-atlas-of-taste) by Rajat Parr, Jordan Mackay

A comprehensive guide to the great wines of Europe that explores how and why they taste as they do. The book examines geographical and geological differences, cultural shifts, and producer philosophies across various subregions and terroirs.

### [The 22 Immutable Laws of Marketing](https://elitereads.com/book/the-22-immutable-laws-of-marketing) by Al Ries, Jack Trout

Al Ries and Jack Trout present 22 essential laws that govern marketing success and failure. The book argues that marketing is a battle of perceptions, not products, and provides practical rules for building brands and dominating categories. Using historical examples and strategic insights, the authors outline the foundational principles for understanding consumer behavior in a competitive marketplace.

### [Don't Shoot the Dog!](https://elitereads.com/book/dont-shoot-the-dog) by Karen Pryor

A practical guide to the principles of operant conditioning and behavior modification. Karen Pryor explains how to use positive reinforcement to shape behavior in animals and humans, offering techniques for training without coercion or punishment.

### [The 80/20 Principle](https://elitereads.com/book/the-80-20-principle) by Richard Koch

This book explores the Pareto Principle, which posits that 80 percent of results stem from 20 percent of efforts. Richard Koch demonstrates how to identify and leverage this imbalance across business and personal life to increase effectiveness and simplify decision-making.

### [Stranger in a Strange Land](https://elitereads.com/book/stranger-in-a-strange-land) by Robert A. Heinlein

Valentine Michael Smith, a human born on Mars and raised by Martians, returns to Earth as an adult. The novel follows his attempts to navigate human society, eventually becoming a messianic figure who introduces Martian philosophy and telepathic abilities to humanity. It explores complex themes of religion, sexuality, and the constraints of terrestrial culture.

### [Vagabonding](https://elitereads.com/book/vagabonding) by Rolf Potts

A practical and philosophical guide to the art of long-term world travel. It explores how to finance, plan, and adjust to life on the road while emphasizing simplicity, independence, and an uncommon outlook on time and freedom.

### [Reckless](https://elitereads.com/book/reckless-ed-brubaker) by Ed Brubaker, Sean Phillips

Ethan Reckless is a former 1960s radical and undercover FBI agent turned fixer-for-hire in 1980s Los Angeles. When a fugitive from his past reaches out for help, he is drawn into a web of crime and betrayal that forces him to confront his own history.

### [Poor Charlie's Almanack](https://elitereads.com/book/poor-charlies-almanack) by Charles T. Munger

A collection of speeches and essays by the billionaire vice-chairman of Berkshire Hathaway that outlines his multidisciplinary 'latticework' of mental models. The book provides deep insights into rational decision-making, the psychology of human misjudgment, and the pursuit of worldly wisdom. It remains a foundational text for investors and thinkers seeking to understand the synthesis of business, economics, and psychology.

### [Gold](https://elitereads.com/book/gold-rumi) by Rumi

A vibrant selection of poems by the 13th-century Persian mystic Rumi, newly translated to capture the ecstatic energy and radical intelligence of the original Farsi. The collection focuses on themes of spiritual liberation, divine love, and the transcendence of the self. This edition highlights the musicality and lyrical power that have made Rumi a cornerstone of world literature.

### [The Essays of Warren Buffett: Lessons for Corporate America](https://elitereads.com/book/the-essays-of-warren-buffett-lessons-for-corporate-america) by Warren Buffett, Lawrence A. Cunningham

A curated collection of Warren Buffett’s annual shareholder letters, organized by topic to provide a comprehensive view of his investment philosophy. The book details fundamental principles regarding corporate governance, finance, accounting, and ethical business practices.

### [Warren Buffett's Ground Rules](https://elitereads.com/book/warren-buffetts-ground-rules) by Jeremy C. Miller

Jeremy Miller analyzes Warren Buffett's letters to his partners from 1956 to 1970, revealing the fundamental investment principles and mindset established early in his career. The book extracts the core guidelines that guided Buffett Partnership Limited, providing a framework for disciplined, long-term capital allocation.

### [The Moment of Lift](https://elitereads.com/book/the-moment-of-lift) by Melinda French Gates

Melinda Gates advocates for women's empowerment as the primary lever for lifting societies out of poverty and inequality. Drawing on twenty years of philanthropic work with the Gates Foundation, she explores the connection between gender equity and global progress. The text combines personal anecdotes from her career and marriage with data-driven insights into systemic barriers facing women worldwide.

### [The Outsiders](https://elitereads.com/book/the-outsiders-william-thorndike) by William N. Thorndike

This book profiles eight CEOs who achieved extraordinary long-term returns through a disciplined and unconventional approach to capital allocation. It examines how these leaders prioritized per-share value and cash flow over traditional growth metrics and charismatic management.

### [First a Dream](https://elitereads.com/book/first-a-dream) by Jim Clayton, Bill Retherford

The autobiography of Jim Clayton, detailing his life from humble beginnings as a sharecropper's son to the founding and growth of Clayton Homes. The narrative covers his business principles, entrepreneurial struggles, and the eventual multi-billion dollar acquisition of his company by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway.

### [The Making of the President 1960](https://elitereads.com/book/the-making-of-the-president-1960) by Theodore H. White

A detailed account of the 1960 U.S. presidential election between John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon. It analyzes the campaign strategies, primary battles, and the first-ever televised debates, establishing a new style of modern political journalism.

### [The Little Book of Common Sense Investing](https://elitereads.com/book/the-little-book-of-common-sense-investing) by John C. Bogle

John C. Bogle, the founder of Vanguard, outlines why low-cost index funds are the most effective way for individuals to build long-term wealth. He explains that active management often fails to beat market averages once fees and taxes are considered. The book provides a fundamental guide to asset allocation and the mathematical certainty of passive investing.

### [Tap Dancing to Work](https://elitereads.com/book/tap-dancing-to-work) by Carol J. Loomis

A collection of Fortune magazine articles and commentary spanning several decades that chronicles the career and investment philosophy of Warren Buffett. It provides insights into his strategies for management, philanthropy, and public policy through the lens of journalist and close friend Carol Loomis.

### [Stress Test](https://elitereads.com/book/stress-test-reflections-on-financial-crises) by Timothy F. Geithner

Timothy Geithner's memoir provides an insider's account of the response to the 2008 financial crisis. He describes the high-stakes decision-making processes at the Federal Reserve and the Treasury aimed at preventing a second Great Depression.

### [How to Win Friends and Influence People](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-win-friends-and-influence-people) by Dale Carnegie

A foundational self-help work that outlines core principles for effective communication and relationship building. It provides practical techniques for influencing others through empathy, appreciation, and understanding human psychology.

### [Shoe Dog](https://elitereads.com/book/shoe-dog) by Phil Knight

Phil Knight, the founder of Nike, details his journey from selling Japanese running shoes out of the trunk of his car to building a global athletic empire. The memoir chronicles the early struggles, strategic risks, and the eccentric team of misfits who shaped the brand. It provides a candid look at the challenges and personal costs of entrepreneurship.

### [Personal History](https://elitereads.com/book/personal-history) by Katharine Graham

The memoir of Katharine Graham, the former publisher of The Washington Post who oversaw the paper during the Watergate scandal and the publication of the Pentagon Papers. It chronicles her journey from a sheltered upbringing to becoming one of the most powerful women in American media. The narrative provides an inside look at the intersection of power, politics, and journalism in the 20th century.

### [Jack: Straight from the Gut](https://elitereads.com/book/jack-straight-from-the-gut) by Jack Welch, John A. Byrne

The autobiography of Jack Welch, the legendary CEO of General Electric, detailing his career and the management principles that drove the company's growth. It explores his 'straight from the gut' approach to leadership, the implementation of Six Sigma, and the cultural transformation of GE.

### [The Intelligent Investor](https://elitereads.com/book/the-intelligent-investor) by Benjamin Graham

A foundational guide to value investing that teaches investors how to develop long-term strategies and minimize risk. It introduces key concepts like the 'margin of safety' and the 'Mr. Market' metaphor to illustrate market volatility and investor psychology. The revised edition includes updated commentary that applies Graham's principles to modern financial markets.

### [Bull!: A History of the Boom and Bust, 1982-2004](https://elitereads.com/book/bull-a-history-of-the-boom-and-bust-1982-2004) by Maggie Mahar

A historical account of the massive growth in the U.S. stock market from 1982 through the early 2000s. Financial journalist Maggie Mahar analyzes the key figures and psychological factors that fueled the dot-com bubble and the eventual market correction.

### [Essays in Persuasion](https://elitereads.com/book/essays-in-persuasion) by John Maynard Keynes

A collection of essays and articles written by Keynes between 1919 and 1931. The book covers his critiques of the Versailles Treaty, his warnings about inflation and deflation, and his vision for the future of economic prosperity.

### [Where Are the Customers' Yachts?](https://elitereads.com/book/where-are-the-customers-yachts) by Fred Schwed Jr.

A satirical critique of Wall Street culture and the investment industry, originally published in 1940. It humorously explores how financial professionals prosper while their clients often lose money, highlighting the timeless folly and psychology of human nature in financial markets.

### [Take on the Street](https://elitereads.com/book/take-on-the-street) by Arthur Levitt

Arthur Levitt, the former chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, offers an insider's perspective on the conflicts of interest within the financial industry. The book provides guidance for individual investors on navigating broker recommendations, mutual fund fees, and corporate accounting practices.

### [Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits](https://elitereads.com/book/common-stocks-and-uncommon-profits) by Philip Fisher

Fisher outlines a qualitative approach to growth investing, centered on finding companies with exceptional long-term potential. He presents the 'Fifteen Points' for stock evaluation and the 'scuttlebutt' method for gathering business intelligence. The text emphasizes management quality, research and development, and the benefits of long-term ownership over market timing.

### [The Great Crash 1929](https://elitereads.com/book/the-great-crash-1929) by John Kenneth Galbraith

A classic economic history of the lead-up to the Wall Street crash of 1929 and the subsequent financial collapse. Galbraith analyzes the rampant speculation, systemic vulnerabilities, and the psychology of market manias that triggered the Great Depression.

### [A Few Lessons for Investors and Managers](https://elitereads.com/book/a-few-lessons-for-investors-and-managers) by Peter Bevelin

Peter Bevelin distills Warren Buffett's wisdom from annual reports and speeches into a concise guide for managers and investors. The book explores principles of business valuation, risk reduction, and the importance of trustworthy management. It emphasizes the synergy between being a disciplined businessman and a successful investor.

### [Dream Big](https://elitereads.com/book/dream-big-cristiane-correa) by Cristiane Correa

Dream Big chronicles the rise of Brazilian entrepreneurs Jorge Paulo Lemann, Marcel Telles, and Beto Sicupira, the trio behind 3G Capital. The narrative details their management philosophy centered on meritocracy and aggressive cost-cutting, which facilitated the acquisition of global brands like Anheuser-Busch, Burger King, and Heinz.

### [Limping on Water](https://elitereads.com/book/limping-on-water) by Phil Beuth

Phil Beuth’s memoir chronicles his forty-year career at Capital Cities Communications, rising from the company's first employee to a top executive at ABC. Born with cerebral palsy, Beuth shares insights into the growth of the media industry and the leadership principles that guided one of America's most successful communications companies.

### [Business Adventures](https://elitereads.com/book/business-adventures-twelve-classic-tales-from-the-world-of-wall-street) by John Brooks

A collection of twelve essays originally published in The New Yorker, examining pivotal moments in 20th-century American business and finance. The book covers events such as the 1962 stock market crash, the failure of the Ford Edsel, and the rise of Xerox.

### [Nuclear Terrorism](https://elitereads.com/book/nuclear-terrorism) by Graham Allison

Nuclear Terrorism examines the threat of terrorist organizations acquiring and using nuclear weapons. Graham Allison argues that while an attack is likely on the current policy path, it remains preventable through a strategy focused on securing fissile materials and strengthening international non-proliferation efforts.

### [The Smartest Guys in the Room](https://elitereads.com/book/the-smartest-guys-in-the-room) by Bethany McLean, Peter Elkind

A detailed account of the rise and fall of the Enron Corporation, examining the systemic accounting fraud and corporate greed that led to one of the largest bankruptcies in U.S. history. Based on extensive research and interviews, the book explores the culture of deception and the roles of key executives like Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. It provides a comprehensive analysis of the corporate governance and ethical failures behind the company's collapse.

### [In an Uncertain World](https://elitereads.com/book/in-an-uncertain-world) by Robert E. Rubin, Jacob Weisberg

A memoir by former U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, detailing his tenure during the Clinton administration and his previous career at Goldman Sachs. The book explains his philosophy of probabilistic thinking and its application to high-stakes financial crises and economic policy.

### [In the Plex: How Google Thinks, Works, and Shapes Our Lives](https://elitereads.com/book/in-the-plex) by Steven Levy

An investigative look at Google's history, engineering culture, and business philosophy. Based on internal access to the company, the book details how its algorithmic focus and founding vision reshaped the internet and global information systems.

### [The Selfish Gene](https://elitereads.com/book/the-selfish-gene) by Richard Dawkins

Richard Dawkins presents a gene-centered view of evolution, proposing that genes are the fundamental units of selection. The work explores how genetic self-interest drives biological processes and introduces the concept of the meme as a unit of cultural transmission.

### [Models of My Life](https://elitereads.com/book/models-of-my-life) by Herbert A. Simon

An autobiography by Nobel laureate Herbert A. Simon, detailing his interdisciplinary career in economics, psychology, and computer science. The narrative explores the concept of bounded rationality and uses the metaphor of a maze to describe the search for solutions in life and science. It documents the foundations of artificial intelligence and the transformation of modern organizational theory.

### [Living within Limits](https://elitereads.com/book/living-within-limits-garrett-hardin) by Garrett Hardin

Garrett Hardin argues that biological principles of carrying capacity must govern human population and economic activity. He critiques the notion of infinite growth on a finite planet and examines the cultural and political taboos that prevent open discussion of population control.

### [Darwin's Blind Spot](https://elitereads.com/book/darwins-blind-spot) by Frank Ryan

Ryan examines the limitations of natural selection by highlighting the critical role of symbiosis and cooperation in the development of life. The book argues that interactions between species and within the genome are essential drivers of evolution, challenging the traditional focus on individual competition.

### [Titan: The Life of John D. Rockefeller, Sr.](https://elitereads.com/book/titan-the-life-of-john-d-rockefeller-sr) by Ron Chernow

The first full-length biography of John D. Rockefeller, Sr. based on unrestricted access to his private papers. It traces his rise from modest origins to becoming the world's first billionaire and the creator of the Standard Oil monopoly. The narrative explores his complex duality as both a ruthless industrialist and a prolific philanthropist who transformed American medicine and education.

### [Einstein: His Life and Universe](https://elitereads.com/book/einstein-his-life-and-universe) by Walter Isaacson

This definitive biography explores the life and legacy of Albert Einstein, focusing on how his rebellious nature fueled his scientific imagination. Drawing on newly released personal papers, the narrative examines his personal relationships and political views alongside his revolutionary contributions to physics.

### [The Language Instinct](https://elitereads.com/book/the-language-instinct) by Steven Pinker

Steven Pinker argues that language is an innate human biological instinct rather than a cultural invention. Drawing on cognitive science and linguistics, the book explains how children acquire language and how linguistic abilities evolved through natural selection.

### [Guns, Germs, and Steel](https://elitereads.com/book/guns-germs-and-steel) by Jared Diamond

This work explores how geographical and environmental factors, rather than intellectual or genetic differences, shaped the historical development of human societies. It examines how the domestication of plants and animals led to the technological and social advantages that allowed certain civilizations to dominate others.

### [The Warren Buffett Portfolio](https://elitereads.com/book/the-warren-buffett-portfolio-robert-g-hagstrom) by Robert G. Hagstrom

A guide to focus investing that explains Warren Buffett's strategy of maintaining a concentrated portfolio of high-probability stocks. The book details the mathematical and psychological frameworks required to manage a focused investment strategy and achieve long-term market outperformance.

### [The Wealth and Poverty of Nations: Why Some Are So Rich and Some So Poor](https://elitereads.com/book/the-wealth-and-poverty-of-nations) by David S. Landes

A comprehensive study of the historical and cultural reasons behind the economic divergence of nations. David S. Landes analyzes why certain regions flourished while others stagnated, highlighting the roles of technology, institutional frameworks, and social values.

### [Only the Paranoid Survive](https://elitereads.com/book/only-the-paranoid-survive) by Andrew S. Grove

This management classic explores the concept of Strategic Inflection Points—moments of massive change that can make or break a business. Former Intel CEO Andrew Grove shares strategies for identifying these transitions and navigating companies through periods of intense competition and technological disruption.

### [A Matter of Degrees: What Temperature Reveals about the Past and Future of Our Species, Planet, and Universe](https://elitereads.com/book/a-matter-of-degrees-gino-segre) by Gino Segrè

Physicist Gino Segrè explores the fundamental role of temperature across biological, physical, and cosmic scales. The book examines how thermal laws influence human evolution, planetary geology, and the origins of the universe while detailing the historical development of the thermometer and thermodynamics.

### [Master of the Game](https://elitereads.com/book/master-of-the-game-connie-bruck) by Connie Bruck

### [A Universe from Nothing](https://elitereads.com/book/a-universe-from-nothing) by Lawrence M. Krauss

Physicist Lawrence Krauss explores how modern cosmology and quantum mechanics suggest the universe could have arisen from nothing without supernatural intervention. He describes the role of dark energy and the Higgs boson to explain the scientific evidence behind cosmic origins.

### [The Third Chimpanzee](https://elitereads.com/book/the-third-chimpanzee) by Jared Diamond

An investigation into the biological and cultural origins of the human species, exploring the small genetic gap between humans and chimpanzees. It analyzes the emergence of language, art, and complex social structures while addressing humanity's propensity for environmental destruction and genocide.

### [Yes!](https://elitereads.com/book/yes-50-scientifically-proven-ways-to-be-persuasive) by Noah J. Goldstein, Steve J. Martin, Robert B. Cialdini

A collection of fifty research-based strategies for increasing influence and persuasion in professional and personal life. The book distills complex psychological studies into brief, actionable chapters focused on how small changes in communication can lead to significant shifts in behavior.

### [Judgment in Managerial Decision Making](https://elitereads.com/book/judgment-in-managerial-decision-making) by Max H. Bazerman, Don A. Moore

This book examines the cognitive biases and heuristics that influence managerial judgment in complex organizational environments. It provides practical strategies for improving decision-making processes through insights from behavioral decision research, covering topics such as negotiation, investment mistakes, and ethical awareness.

### [The Blind Watchmaker](https://elitereads.com/book/the-blind-watchmaker) by Richard Dawkins

Richard Dawkins explains the theory of evolution by natural selection as a 'blind watchmaker' that generates biological complexity without a conscious designer. He systematically addresses arguments for creationism and demonstrates how gradual adaptation over geological timescales accounts for the diversity of life.

### [Barbarians at the Gate](https://elitereads.com/book/barbarians-at-the-gate) by Bryan Burrough, John Helyar

### [Genome: The Autobiography of a Species in 23 Chapters](https://elitereads.com/book/genome-the-autobiography-of-a-species-in-23-chapters) by Matt Ridley

An exploration of the human genome structured into 23 chapters, each dedicated to one pair of human chromosomes. The book examines the evolutionary history, biological function, and philosophical implications of specific genes to explain the blueprint of the human species.

### [The Martians of Science: Five Physicists Who Changed the Twentieth Century](https://elitereads.com/book/the-martians-of-science-five-physicists-who-changed-the-twentieth-century) by István Hargittai

A collective biography of five Hungarian-born scientists—Theodore von Kármán, Leo Szilard, Eugene Wigner, John von Neumann, and Edward Teller—who escaped fascism to redefine modern physics. ### [Three Scientists and Their Gods: Looking for Meaning in an Age of Information](https://elitereads.com/book/three-scientists-and-their-gods) by Robert Wright

### [Ice Age](https://elitereads.com/book/ice-age-john-gribbin-mary-gribbin) by John Gribbin, Mary Gribbin

### [Conspiracy of Fools](https://elitereads.com/book/conspiracy-of-fools) by Kurt Eichenwald

### [Martyr!](https://elitereads.com/book/martyr-kaveh-akbar) by Kaveh Akbar

### [The Three-Body Problem](https://elitereads.com/book/the-three-body-problem) by Cixin Liu

During China's Cultural Revolution, an astrophysicist sends a signal into deep space that is received by an alien civilization on a dying planet. Decades later, a nanomaterials researcher uncovers a conspiracy involving a virtual reality game that serves as a recruitment tool for those welcoming an extraterrestrial invasion. The story follows humanity's attempt to respond to the threat of a fleet traveling from an unstable trinary star system.

### [The Book of Records](https://elitereads.com/book/the-book-of-records) by Madeleine Thien

Lina and her father seek refuge in a mysterious enclave called the Sea, a staging post where past and future timelines intersect. In this shape-shifting building, they encounter the avatars of historical thinkers like Baruch Spinoza, Hannah Arendt, and Du Fu. The narrative explores the migratory nature of humanity and the quest for home amidst political and personal catastrophe.

### [Orbital](https://elitereads.com/book/orbital-samantha-harvey) by Samantha Harvey

Chronicles a single day in the lives of six astronauts aboard the International Space Station as they experience sixteen sunrises and sunsets. The narrative serves as a meditative reflection on the beauty and fragility of Earth, human connection, and existential themes.

### [Team of Rivals: The Political Genius of Abraham Lincoln](https://elitereads.com/book/team-of-rivals) by Doris Kearns Goodwin

A biographical study of Abraham Lincoln and the cabinet of former political opponents he assembled during the American Civil War. The book explores how Lincoln's emotional intelligence and leadership enabled him to reconcile conflicting personalities to preserve the Union and abolish slavery.

### [The Anthropologists](https://elitereads.com/book/the-anthropologists) by Ayşegül Savaş

Asya and Manu, a young couple living in an unnamed foreign city, search for an apartment while navigating their status as expats. A documentary filmmaker by trade, Asya observes her neighborhood's daily rhythms and local customs to define what constitutes a home and family.

### [Stolen Pride](https://elitereads.com/book/stolen-pride) by Arlie Russell Hochschild

Sociologist Arlie Russell Hochschild examines the emotional and economic landscape of Appalachia to understand the political shift toward the right. The work explores the 'pride paradox' where personal responsibility for systemic failure transforms into collective resentment and political blame.

### [Rosarita](https://elitereads.com/book/rosarita) by Anita Desai

While studying Spanish in San Miguel, Mexico, a young Indian woman named Bonita is approached by a stranger who claims to have known her mother as a traveling artist. Despite remembering her mother as a reserved woman who never left India, Bonita embarks on a journey across Mexico to reconcile these conflicting identities. The novella examines the fluid nature of memory and the historical parallels between the Partition of India and the Mexican Revolution.

### [Growth: A Reckoning](https://elitereads.com/book/growth-daniel-susskind) by Daniel Susskind

Explores the historical origins and evolution of economic growth, arguing that while growth has lifted billions out of poverty, it has also caused environmental destruction and inequality. Susskind contends that growth is driven by the infinite world of ideas and must be redirected to align with human values rather than being abandoned.

### [Poverty, by America](https://elitereads.com/book/poverty-by-america) by Matthew Desmond

Sociologist Matthew Desmond examines why the United States, the wealthiest nation on earth, has higher poverty rates than other advanced democracies. He argues that poverty persists because affluent Americans benefit from it through exploitation in housing and labor markets, as well as tax policies that prioritize the subsidization of wealth. Desmond calls for a collective movement of 'poverty abolitionists' to dismantle these systemic barriers and foster shared prosperity.

### [Who Is Government?](https://elitereads.com/book/who-is-government) by Michael Lewis

A collection of profiles highlighting the essential and often unrecognized work of federal government employees. Edited by Michael Lewis, the book features essays by renowned authors exploring the roles of public servants in agencies like the IRS, NASA, and the Department of Labor.

### [The Work of Art](https://elitereads.com/book/the-work-of-art-adam-moss) by Adam Moss

Former magazine editor Adam Moss explores the creative process through conversations with over 40 artists across various disciplines. The book traces the evolution of specific works from initial sketches and notes to finished masterpieces, revealing the psychological and practical labor behind art-making.

### [The Buffalo Hunter Hunter](https://elitereads.com/book/the-buffalo-hunter-hunter) by Stephen Graham Jones

A historical horror novel centered on the transcribed confessions of a Blackfeet vampire named Good Stab.
