### [Self-Reliance](https://elitereads.com/book/self-reliance-ralph-waldo-emerson) by Ralph Waldo Emerson

A foundational essay of American Transcendentalism that advocates for individualism and the primary importance of trusting one's own intuition. Emerson argues against societal conformity and the blind following of tradition, urging readers to cultivate self-sufficiency and authenticity.

### [The Wager](https://elitereads.com/book/the-wager-david-grann) by David Grann

### [King of Ashes](https://elitereads.com/book/king-of-ashes) by S.A. Cosby

### [Reading Genesis](https://elitereads.com/book/reading-genesis) by Marilynne Robinson

Marilynne Robinson provides a literary and theological interpretation of the Book of Genesis, focusing on its greatness as literature and its exploration of theodicy. She explores themes of divine providence and human fallibility through a close reading of the biblical text.

### [Superintelligence](https://elitereads.com/book/superintelligence-nick-bostrom) by Nick Bostrom

This book explores the potential development of machine intelligence that surpasses human cognitive performance across all domains. It examines the various paths to achieving such systems, the associated risks to humanity, and strategies for ensuring their goals remain aligned with human interests.

### [The Wealth of Nations](https://elitereads.com/book/the-wealth-of-nations) by Adam Smith

A foundational treatise on modern economics that describes the mechanisms of wealth creation and the benefits of free-market competition. Smith introduces the concept of the 'invisible hand' and explores how the division of labor increases productivity while critiquing mercantilist policies.

### [The Storm of Steel](https://elitereads.com/book/the-storm-of-steel) by Ernst Jünger

### [Lying](https://elitereads.com/book/lying-sam-harris) by Sam Harris

### [Masters of Doom](https://elitereads.com/book/masters-of-doom) by David Kushner

The true story of John Carmack and John Romero, the founders of id Software who revolutionized the gaming industry with Doom and Quake. The narrative explores the intersection of subculture, technology, and mainstream entertainment.

### [Waiting for Godot](https://elitereads.com/book/waiting-for-godot) by Samuel Beckett

Two characters, Vladimir and Estragon, wait on a desolate road for the arrival of a mysterious figure named Godot, who never appears. Their repetitive dialogue and encounters with other travelers explore themes of existential uncertainty and the struggle for meaning. The play is a definitive work of the Theatre of the Absurd and a landmark of 20th-century drama.

### [The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress](https://elitereads.com/book/the-moon-is-a-harsh-mistress) by Robert A. Heinlein

A 2075 lunar penal colony revolts against Earth's authority. Three human leaders and a self-aware supercomputer coordinate an independence movement while navigating complex social and political structures. The novel examines libertarian theory and the logistics of a lunar-based revolution.

### [The Machine Stops](https://elitereads.com/book/the-machine-stops) by E.M. Forster

A science fiction story depicting a future where humanity lives in isolated underground cells and depends entirely on a global 'Machine' for survival. The narrative follows a mother and son as they experience the societal and physical consequences of total technological dependency. The work is notable for its prescient descriptions of instant messaging, the internet, and video conferencing.

### [Foundation](https://elitereads.com/book/foundation) by Isaac Asimov

Mathematician Hari Seldon predicts the collapse of the Galactic Empire and establishes a colony called the Foundation to preserve human knowledge and minimize the duration of the coming dark ages. ### [The Road to Serfdom](https://elitereads.com/book/the-road-to-serfdom) by F. A. Hayek

### [King Lear](https://elitereads.com/book/king-lear) by William Shakespeare

Ray Dalio shares the unconventional principles he developed while building Bridgewater Associates into one of the world's largest hedge funds. The book provides a framework for decision-making based on radical truth and radical transparency, viewing both life and organizations as machines that can be understood and optimized.

### [River Out of Eden: A Darwinian View of Life](https://elitereads.com/book/river-out-of-eden-richard-dawkins) by Richard Dawkins

This work explores evolutionary biology through the metaphor of a digital river of DNA flowing through time. It explains how genetic information persists across generations and outlines the mechanisms of natural selection and common ancestry.

### [Steve Jobs](https://elitereads.com/book/steve-jobs) by Walter Isaacson

Based on more than forty interviews with Steve Jobs and over a hundred conversations with his inner circle and competitors, this biography provides an unvarnished look at the life of the Apple co-founder. It traces Jobs's professional journey and intense personality, highlighting his role in revolutionizing multiple industries including personal computing, music, and mobile technology.

### [Creativity and the Brain](https://elitereads.com/book/creativity-and-the-brain) by Mario Tokoro, Ken Mogi

An exploration of human creativity through the lens of modern brain science, utilizing tools such as EEG, EMG, and fMRI. The text examines the brain as a complex system and presents scientific theories for analyzing and synthesizing creative processes.

### [The Meaning of Human Existence](https://elitereads.com/book/the-meaning-of-human-existence) by Edward O. Wilson

A Pulitzer Prize-winning biologist explores the origins of humanity and our unique place in the universe. The book integrates science and philosophy to examine evolutionary history, the development of human nature, and the future of the species.

### [The Power of Habit](https://elitereads.com/book/the-power-of-habit) by Charles Duhigg

The book explores the scientific understanding of habit formation and change in individuals, organizations, and societies. It introduces the habit loop—comprising a cue, routine, and reward—and illustrates how identifying these components can lead to behavioral transformation through various case studies.

### [The Hero with a Thousand Faces](https://elitereads.com/book/the-hero-with-a-thousand-faces) by Joseph Campbell

A foundational work of comparative mythology that outlines the 'monomyth' or hero's journey, a universal narrative structure found across diverse cultures and eras. It explores how mythological themes reflect psychological archetypes and the human experience of transformation.

### [Incognito: The Secret Lives of the Brain](https://elitereads.com/book/incognito-the-secret-lives-of-the-brain) by David Eagleman

Neuroscientist David Eagleman explores the hidden unconscious processes that drive human behavior, thoughts, and perceptions. The book examines why the conscious mind is only a small fraction of the brain's activity and how internal neural conflicts shape our identity and legal responsibility.

### [Think Again: The Power of Knowing What You Don't Know](https://elitereads.com/book/think-again-the-power-of-knowing-what-you-dont-know) by Adam Grant

Think Again investigates the science of mental flexibility and the art of rethinking. Adam Grant examines how to develop the capacity to question personal beliefs, embrace the joy of being wrong, and foster a culture of lifelong learning.

### [The Holy Grail of Investing](https://elitereads.com/book/the-holy-grail-of-investing) by Tony Robbins, Christopher Zook

Tony Robbins and Christopher Zook examine the world of alternative investments, including private equity, private credit, and venture capital. Through interviews with elite fund managers, the book outlines strategies used by institutional investors to achieve outsized returns. It serves as a guide for individual investors seeking to navigate high-yield opportunities outside traditional stock and bond markets.

### [Strength in Stillness](https://elitereads.com/book/strength-in-stillness) by Bob Roth

Bob Roth provides a practical guide to Transcendental Meditation, explaining the science behind the technique and its role in reducing toxic stress. The book distinguishes between different meditation styles and highlights the physiological benefits of attaining a state of restful alertness. It features insights and personal anecdotes from various practitioners, ranging from business leaders to artists.

### [The Yellow Pad](https://elitereads.com/book/the-yellow-pad) by Robert E. Rubin

Former U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin outlines his decision-making framework based on 'probabilistic thinking' developed over six decades in finance and government. The book combines personal anecdotes from Wall Street and Washington with philosophical insights on navigating high-stakes choices under uncertainty.

### [Originals: How Non-Conformists Move the World](https://elitereads.com/book/originals-adam-grant) by Adam Grant

Adam Grant examines how individuals can champion new ideas and challenge the status quo without risking everything. The book explores the habits of original thinkers, the importance of strategic timing, and how to build organizational cultures that welcome dissent.

### [The Undoing Project](https://elitereads.com/book/the-undoing-project-a-friendship-that-changed-our-minds) by Michael Lewis

The book explores the revolutionary partnership between Israeli psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky. Their collaboration founded the field of behavioral economics by identifying systematic errors in human judgment and decision-making.

### [Welcome to Your Brain](https://elitereads.com/book/welcome-to-your-brain) by Sandra Aamodt, Sam Wang

Two neuroscientists provide a comprehensive and accessible guide to the human brain, addressing common myths and explaining the science of everyday behaviors. The book covers topics ranging from memory and perception to the physiological effects of aging and lifestyle choices.

### [Destined for War: Can America and China Escape Thucydides's Trap?](https://elitereads.com/book/destined-for-war) by Graham Allison

Graham Allison examines the risk of conflict between the United States and China through the framework of Thucydides's Trap. The book analyzes sixteen historical instances where a rising power challenged a ruling one, identifying factors that led to either war or peaceful coexistence.

### [In Over Our Heads](https://elitereads.com/book/in-over-our-heads) by Robert Kegan

Robert Kegan examines the gap between the complex cognitive demands of contemporary life and our existing mental capacities. He introduces a framework of adult development through 'orders of consciousness,' exploring how we can evolve to meet the challenges of parenting, work, and leadership.

### [Why We Believe in God(s): A Concise Guide to the Science of Faith](https://elitereads.com/book/why-we-believe-in-god-s) by J. Anderson Thomson, Clare Aukofer

An investigation into the evolutionary and psychological origins of religious belief. Using research from cognitive neuroscience, the authors examine mechanisms like agency detection and social cohesion that predispose the human mind to religious thought.

### [From Bacteria to Bach and Back](https://elitereads.com/book/from-bacteria-to-bach-and-back-the-evolution-of-minds) by Daniel C. Dennett

An exploration of the evolutionary origins of human consciousness and the mind. Dennett integrates biological theory with computer science to argue that comprehension and creativity emerged from mindless mechanical processes and the cultural transmission of memes.

### [Accidental Presidents: Eight Men Who Changed America](https://elitereads.com/book/accidental-presidents-eight-men-who-changed-america) by Jared Cohen

An exploration of the eight instances in American history where a vice president ascended to the presidency following the death of the incumbent. The book examines how these unplanned transitions and the character of each successor shaped the nation and the evolution of the executive office.

### [An Everyone Culture](https://elitereads.com/book/an-everyone-culture) by Robert Kegan, Lisa Laskow Lahey

This book explores the concept of Deliberately Developmental Organizations (DDOs), where personal growth is integrated into the daily fabric of work. Kegan and Lahey examine companies that treat human development as a core business strategy to unlock organizational potential.

### [Beyond Religion: Ethics for a Whole World](https://elitereads.com/book/beyond-religion-ethics-for-a-whole-world) by Dalai Lama

The Dalai Lama proposes a system of secular ethics based on universal human values rather than religious dogma. He outlines how compassion and mindfulness can serve as a foundation for a global human community. The book provides practical mental training exercises to cultivate inner peace and ethical mindfulness in a diverse world.

### [Think Like a Monk](https://elitereads.com/book/think-like-a-monk) by Jay Shetty

Jay Shetty distills ancient Vedic wisdom into practical steps for overcoming negativity and finding inner peace in the modern world. The book provides a roadmap for adopting a monk mindset through meditation, habit formation, and identifying one's true purpose.

### [The Evolving Self](https://elitereads.com/book/the-evolving-self) by Robert Kegan

This work explores human development as a lifelong activity of meaning-making, where individuals continuously reconstruct their understanding of self and the world. Kegan utilizes Piagetian theory to describe the internal experience of growth through a series of evolutionary stages and psychological balances.

### [Subliminal](https://elitereads.com/book/subliminal-how-your-unconscious-mind-rules-your-behavior) by Leonard Mlodinow

Leonard Mlodinow explores the new science of the unconscious and how it influences our perception, behavior, and social judgment. The book details how subliminal processes shape our experiences of the world, our relationships, and our decision-making.

### [The Gift of Adversity](https://elitereads.com/book/the-gift-of-adversity-norman-e-rosenthal) by Norman E. Rosenthal

Psychiatrist Norman Rosenthal explores how life's disappointments and difficulties serve as catalysts for personal growth and resilience. Drawing from his own experiences in apartheid South Africa and clinical case studies, the book offers insights into turning setbacks into wisdom.

### [The Rise of the Rest](https://elitereads.com/book/the-rise-of-the-rest) by Steve Case

Steve Case explores the growth of startup ecosystems in American cities outside traditional tech hubs like Silicon Valley. He profiles entrepreneurs rebuilding local economies and argues for the democratization of venture capital to foster national innovation.

### [Who's in Charge?: Free Will and the Science of the Brain](https://elitereads.com/book/whos-in-charge-free-will-and-the-science-of-the-brain) by Michael S. Gazzaniga

Michael S. Gazzaniga explores the intersection of neuroscience and philosophy to address the concept of free will. He argues that while the brain functions through deterministic physical processes, personal responsibility remains a social construct that emerges from human interaction.

### [A Whole New Mind: Why Right-Brainers Will Rule the Future](https://elitereads.com/book/a-whole-new-mind) by Daniel H. Pink

Daniel H. Pink examines the transition from an economy based on logical, 'left-brain' analytical skills to one that prizes creative and empathetic 'right-brain' aptitudes. He identifies six essential human abilities—Design, Story, Symphony, Empathy, Play, and Meaning—that are critical for professional success in the modern era.

### [My Stroke of Insight](https://elitereads.com/book/my-stroke-of-insight) by Jill Bolte Taylor

A neuroanatomist's account of a massive stroke she suffered in her left hemisphere at age thirty-seven. Taylor describes the experience of watching her brain's functions deteriorate and her subsequent eight-year journey to full recovery. The book explores the distinct personalities of the brain's two hemispheres and the insights gained into the nature of consciousness.

### [The Rise and Fall of the Great Powers](https://elitereads.com/book/the-rise-and-fall-of-the-great-powers) by Paul Kennedy

This classic work examines the five-century history of global power dynamics, focusing on the essential link between a nation's economic productivity and its military capabilities. Kennedy introduces the concept of 'imperial overstretch' to explain how dominant states eventually decline when their strategic commitments exceed their economic means.

### [Changing Minds: The Art and Science of Changing Our Own and Other People's Minds](https://elitereads.com/book/changing-minds-howard-gardner) by Howard Gardner

Gardner identifies seven levers—such as resonance, reason, and real-world events—that influence how individuals and groups shift their perspectives. Through diverse case studies of political and business leaders, the book explores the cognitive mechanics behind belief change and the factors that cause mental resistance.

### [Who Am I?: 16 Basic Desires That Motivate Our Actions and Define Our Personalities](https://elitereads.com/book/who-am-i-steven-reiss) by Steven Reiss

Psychologist Steven Reiss presents a research-based framework identifying sixteen fundamental human desires that drive behavior and define personality. The book explains how individuals prioritize these universal motives—such as power, curiosity, and order—to create a unique motivational profile that affects their relationships and professional life.

### [Einstein's Mistakes: The Human Failings of Genius](https://elitereads.com/book/einsteins-mistakes-the-human-failings-of-genius) by Hans C. Ohanian

Hans C. Ohanian examines approximately forty of Albert Einstein's scientific papers that contained significant errors. The book explores how these mistakes, ranging from mathematical blunders to misconceptions about physics, served as essential stepping stones in the development of his revolutionary theories.

### [The Upside of Inequality](https://elitereads.com/book/the-upside-of-inequality) by Edward Conard

Edward Conard argues that income inequality is a byproduct of innovation and risk-taking in a modern economy. The book suggests that high payoffs for success are necessary to drive the economic growth that benefits all layers of society.

### [The Lessons of History](https://elitereads.com/book/the-lessons-of-history) by Will Durant, Ariel Durant

### [The Role of the Individual in History](https://elitereads.com/book/the-role-of-the-individual-in-history) by G.V. Plekhanov

### [The Serengeti Rules](https://elitereads.com/book/the-serengeti-rules) by Sean B. Carroll

### [The Spiritual Brain](https://elitereads.com/book/the-spiritual-brain) by Mario Beauregard, Denyse O'Leary

Neuroscientist Mario Beauregard and journalist Denyse O'Leary explore the relationship between the brain and spiritual experiences. ### [No Rules Rules: Netflix and the Culture of Reinvention](https://elitereads.com/book/no-rules-rules-netflix-and-the-culture-of-reinvention) by Reed Hastings, Erin Meyer

### [Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind](https://elitereads.com/book/positioning-the-battle-for-your-mind) by Al Ries, Jack Trout

### [How Will You Measure Your Life?](https://elitereads.com/book/how-will-you-measure-your-life) by Clayton M. Christensen, James Allworth, Karen Dillon

### [Competing Against Luck](https://elitereads.com/book/competing-against-luck) by Clayton M. Christensen, Taddy Hall, Karen Dillon, David S. Duncan

### [The Innovator's DNA](https://elitereads.com/book/the-innovators-dna) by Jeff Dyer, Hal Gregersen, Clayton M. Christensen

### [Crossing the Chasm](https://elitereads.com/book/crossing-the-chasm) by Geoffrey A. Moore

This marketing classic examines the gap between early adopters and the pragmatic mainstream market for high-tech products. The methodology focuses on niche market dominance and the development of the 'whole product' to satisfy pragmatic customers.

### [High Output Management](https://elitereads.com/book/high-output-management) by Andrew S. Grove

### [Invent and Wander](https://elitereads.com/book/invent-and-wander) by Jeff Bezos, Walter Isaacson

### [Rework](https://elitereads.com/book/rework) by Jason Fried, David Heinemeier Hansson

### [Lights Out](https://elitereads.com/book/lights-out-ted-koppel) by Ted Koppel

### [Good to Great](https://elitereads.com/book/good-to-great) by Jim Collins

### [The Mythical Man-Month](https://elitereads.com/book/the-mythical-man-month) by Frederick P. Brooks Jr.

A personal exploration of the 1960s based on the archival collection of presidential historian Doris Kearns Goodwin and her husband Richard Goodwin. The narrative details their involvement with John F. Kennedy, Lyndon B. Johnson, and the decade's defining political and social upheavals.

### [The Women](https://elitereads.com/book/the-women) by Kristin Hannah

In 1965, nursing student Frankie McGrath joins the Army Nurse Corps to serve in the Vietnam War. The story follows her journey from a naive recruit to a seasoned veteran, exploring the trauma of combat and the struggle for recognition in a divided America.

### [How to Know a Person](https://elitereads.com/book/how-to-know-a-person) by David Brooks

David Brooks provides a practical guide to the art of truly seeing and understanding others. Drawing on fields like psychology and neuroscience, he explores how empathy, curiosity, and active listening can build deeper human connections and counteract social fragmentation.

### [Born a Crime](https://elitereads.com/book/born-a-crime) by Trevor Noah

A memoir detailing the author's upbringing in South Africa during the final years of apartheid. It explores his childhood as a mixed-race boy born to a white father and a black mother, a union that was illegal at the time of his birth. The narrative documents his family's resilience and the systemic absurdity of institutionalized racism.

### [Engineering in Plain Sight](https://elitereads.com/book/engineering-in-plain-sight) by Grady Hillhouse

An illustrated field guide to the human-made world, explaining the engineering principles behind everyday infrastructure. It covers complex systems like the electrical grid, roadways, and water management, demystifying the built environment through clear diagrams and accessible explanations.

### [The Great Influenza](https://elitereads.com/book/the-great-influenza) by John M. Barry

An investigation into the 1918 influenza pandemic, which killed millions worldwide during the height of World War I. Barry chronicles the evolution of the virus alongside the development of modern American medical research and the failure of public officials to tell the truth. The narrative explores how science and policy collided to shape the global response to the crisis.

### [Cloud Atlas](https://elitereads.com/book/cloud-atlas) by David Mitchell

A novel comprising six nested stories that span from the mid-19th century to a post-apocalyptic future. It explores themes of reincarnation and the interconnectedness of human lives through varied literary styles. The narrative structure follows each story to its midpoint before returning to conclude them in reverse chronological order.

### [Educated](https://elitereads.com/book/educated) by Tara Westover

Tara Westover recounts her upbringing in a survivalist Mormon family in rural Idaho, where she was kept out of school and lived without medical records or a birth certificate. The memoir follows her journey to self-education, beginning with her first classroom experience at age 17 and culminating in a PhD from Cambridge University. It explores themes of family loyalty, abuse, and the transformative impact of higher education.

### [Chasing Hope: A Reporter's Life](https://elitereads.com/book/chasing-hope-a-reporters-life) by Nicholas D. Kristof

Two-time Pulitzer Prize winner Nicholas D. Kristof shares an intimate memoir about his storied career as a foreign correspondent and columnist for The New York Times. The narrative recounts his path from an Oregon farm to reporting on major world events, including the Tiananmen Square protests and the Darfur genocide. The book highlights the importance of purpose-driven journalism in exposing global injustice and humanitarian crises.

### [When Everyone Knows That Everyone Knows...](https://elitereads.com/book/when-everyone-knows-that-everyone-knows) by Steven Pinker

An exploration of the concept of 'common knowledge'—the recursive state where everyone knows that everyone else knows. Steven Pinker examines how this phenomenon enables social coordination and explains behaviors ranging from politeness and innuendo to political revolutions and financial bubbles.

### [How the World Really Works](https://elitereads.com/book/how-the-world-really-works) by Vaclav Smil

A quantitative analysis of the physical and technical foundations of modern civilization, focusing on energy systems, food production, and material science. Smil evaluates the complexities of globalization and the environment to provide a realistic assessment of current global challenges.

### [Why We're Polarized](https://elitereads.com/book/why-were-polarized) by Ezra Klein

An analysis of the structural and psychological forces driving political polarization in the United States. Journalist Ezra Klein explores how partisan identities have merged with social and cultural identities, creating a feedback loop that sustains a dysfunctional political system.

### [The Power](https://elitereads.com/book/the-power-naomi-alderman) by Naomi Alderman

In this speculative novel, teenage girls suddenly develop the ability to emit lethal electrical shocks from their hands, a power that quickly spreads to older women. The story examines the resulting global shift in gender roles and the nature of power through the perspectives of four individuals.

### [Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow](https://elitereads.com/book/tomorrow-and-tomorrow-and-tomorrow) by Gabrielle Zevin

A sprawling narrative following the thirty-year friendship and creative partnership of Sam Masur and Sadie Green, two video game designers who achieve global stardom. The story explores the complexities of their connection, creative ambitions, and the intersection of virtual and real-world experiences. It examines themes of disability, identity, and the enduring nature of collaborative love.

### [Not the End of the World](https://elitereads.com/book/not-the-end-of-the-world) by Hannah Ritchie

Data scientist Hannah Ritchie provides a data-driven analysis of global environmental issues to show that humanity is making significant progress toward sustainability. She examines topics like climate change, air pollution, and deforestation to offer evidence-based solutions and a more optimistic perspective on the future. The book challenges doomsday narratives by highlighting the specific actions and technologies that are already working.

### [Relativity: The Special and the General Theory](https://elitereads.com/book/relativity-the-special-and-the-general-theory) by Albert Einstein

Albert Einstein explains the special and general theories of relativity for readers without advanced mathematical training. Using thought experiments and simple analogies, he describes the relationship between space, time, and gravity.

### [Ideas and Opinions](https://elitereads.com/book/ideas-and-opinions-albert-einstein) by Albert Einstein

A comprehensive collection of Albert Einstein's non-technical writings, gathered under his own supervision. It features essays, articles, and letters regarding the theory of relativity, alongside his perspectives on pacifism, social justice, and the relationship between science and religion.

### [The Evolution of Physics](https://elitereads.com/book/the-evolution-of-physics) by Albert Einstein, Leopold Infeld

A comprehensive narrative tracing the progression of physical theories from early mechanical views to the development of relativity and quantum physics. Written for a general audience, it explores the logical connection between concepts like field, energy, and matter without relying on complex mathematical formulas.

### [The World As I See It](https://elitereads.com/book/the-world-as-i-see-it) by Albert Einstein

A collection of letters, speeches, and essays exploring Albert Einstein's views on humanity, science, and the political landscape of the early 20th century. It documents his thoughts on relativity, pacifism, and his personal philosophy regarding religion and society.

### [The Meaning of Relativity](https://elitereads.com/book/the-meaning-of-relativity) by Albert Einstein

Based on Einstein’s 1921 Stafford Little Lectures at Princeton University, this work provides a technical overview of both special and general relativity. It details the mathematical foundations of the theory, including the development of tensor calculus and the relativistic theory of gravitation.

### [Autobiographical Notes](https://elitereads.com/book/autobiographical-notes) by Albert Einstein

Writing at age 67, Albert Einstein reflects on the evolution of his scientific worldview and intellectual development. The text covers his early fascination with geometry, the influence of philosophical thinkers like Mach and Hume, and the conceptual journey toward the theories of relativity.

### [Out of My Later Years](https://elitereads.com/book/out-of-my-later-years) by Albert Einstein

A collection of essays and addresses by Albert Einstein from 1934 to 1950. The work explores his thoughts on science, ethics, education, and his political views on Zionism and the threat of nuclear war.

### [The Brothers Karamazov](https://elitereads.com/book/the-brothers-karamazov) by Fyodor Dostoevsky

Set in 19th-century Russia, the novel centers on the murder of a brutal landowner and the subsequent investigation involving his four sons. Through their conflicting worldviews, the story explores profound philosophical questions regarding faith, free will, and the origins of morality.

### [Ethics](https://elitereads.com/book/ethics-baruch-spinoza) by Baruch Spinoza

A landmark work of 17th-century rationalism, Spinoza’s masterpiece presents a comprehensive philosophical system using a rigorous geometric method. It defines the nature of God as a single infinite substance, explores the relationship between mind and body, and offers a guide to achieving human freedom through the power of reason and the understanding of emotions.

### [A Treatise of Human Nature](https://elitereads.com/book/a-treatise-of-human-nature) by David Hume

A foundational work of Enlightenment philosophy that examines the origins of human ideas, the nature of causality, and the basis of moral judgment. David Hume applies an empirical method to investigate the psychological foundations of the human mind and its perceptions.

### [Critique of Pure Reason](https://elitereads.com/book/critique-of-pure-reason) by Immanuel Kant

An investigation into the limits and scope of human reason, determining how knowledge is possible independent of experience. Kant synthesizes rationalism and empiricism to introduce transcendental idealism, focusing on the structures of the mind that shape perception.

### [Don Quixote](https://elitereads.com/book/don-quixote) by Miguel de Cervantes

An aging Spanish nobleman, Alonso Quijano, loses his mind from reading too many chivalric romances and sets out to revive knighthood under the name Don Quixote. Accompanied by his simple squire Sancho Panza, he roams 16th-century Spain on a quest for glory that frequently descends into tragicomic delusion. It is widely considered the first modern novel and a cornerstone of Western literature.

### [A System of Logic](https://elitereads.com/book/a-system-of-logic) by John Stuart Mill

A foundational treatise in the philosophy of science that systematizes the principles of inductive reasoning and empirical investigation. Mill argues that all knowledge is derived from experience, providing a comprehensive framework for applying scientific methodology to social and moral questions.

### [Faust](https://elitereads.com/book/faust) by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

A jaded scholar named Faust makes a wager with the devil, Mephistopheles, offering his soul in exchange for unlimited knowledge and worldly pleasures. The drama follows his pursuit of meaning through various experiences, leading to a tragic romance and eventual spiritual conflict.

### [Parerga and Paralipomena](https://elitereads.com/book/parerga-and-paralipomena) by Arthur Schopenhauer

A collection of philosophical essays and reflections published late in Schopenhauer's life, intended as supplements to his major work. It contains his most accessible writings, including 'Aphorisms on the Wisdom of Life,' covering topics from ethics and metaphysics to aesthetics and social behavior.

### [Naturwissenschaftliche Volksbücher](https://elitereads.com/book/naturwissenschaftliche-volksbuecher) by Aaron Bernstein

A seminal 19th-century collection of essays that made complex physical and natural sciences accessible to the general public. The work covers fundamental principles of physics, astronomy, and biology, and is famously cited by Albert Einstein as a primary intellectual influence during his childhood.

### [The Grammar of Science](https://elitereads.com/book/the-grammar-of-science) by Karl Pearson

A landmark work in the philosophy of science that argues for the unity of science through its method rather than its subject matter. It explores the relationship between perceptions, scientific laws, and physical concepts like space, time, and matter, significantly influencing the development of modern physics.

### [Mental Radio](https://elitereads.com/book/mental-radio-upton-sinclair) by Upton Sinclair

Upton Sinclair documents a series of telepathic experiments conducted with his second wife, Mary Craig Sinclair. The book details her attempts to mentally replicate hundreds of drawings made by others from separate rooms and includes an appreciative preface by Albert Einstein.

### [Clearing the Air](https://elitereads.com/book/clearing-the-air-hannah-ritchie) by Hannah Ritchie

Hannah Ritchie addresses fifty key questions about climate change using a data-driven approach. The book examines progress in renewable energy, food systems, and technology to provide a pragmatic overview of global environmental challenges.

### [Nexus](https://elitereads.com/book/nexus-a-brief-history-of-information-networks-from-the-stone-age-to-ai) by Yuval Noah Harari

A historical analysis of information networks and their influence on human societies from oral traditions to the rise of artificial intelligence. It examines the relationship between information systems, truth, and power, and how bureaucracy and mythology drive human cooperation. The text addresses the urgent societal and existential choices posed by the rapid development of non-human intelligence.

### [Who Knew: My Story](https://elitereads.com/book/who-knew-my-story) by Barry Diller

In this candid memoir, media mogul Barry Diller recounts his career leading major companies including ABC, Paramount, Fox, and IAC. He provides a revealing account of the deals that shaped American culture and, for the first time, discusses his private life and personal journey.

### [Colorado Springs Notes, 1899–1900](https://elitereads.com/book/colorado-springs-notes-1899-1900) by Nikola Tesla

The research diary of Nikola Tesla from his laboratory in Colorado Springs, documented between June 1899 and January 1900. It details his experiments with high-voltage electrical phenomena and the development of a system for wireless transmission of power.

### [My Inventions: The Autobiography of Nikola Tesla](https://elitereads.com/book/my-inventions-the-autobiography-of-nikola-tesla) by Nikola Tesla

Originally serialized in 1919, this autobiography provides a firsthand account of Nikola Tesla’s life and scientific discoveries. Tesla details his childhood, his unique method of visualizing inventions, and the development of his most significant works, including the alternating current motor and the Tesla coil.

### [The Problem of Increasing Human Energy](https://elitereads.com/book/the-problem-of-increasing-human-energy) by Nikola Tesla

Originally published as a magazine treatise in 1900, this work provides a scientific and philosophical framework for the advancement of humanity. Nikola Tesla explores technical concepts such as wireless power transmission and solar energy alongside his vision for the future of global civilization.

### [The Bible](https://elitereads.com/book/the-bible) by Various

A foundational collection of sacred texts in Judaism and Christianity, composed of the Old and New Testaments. It includes a diverse range of literary forms, including narrative history, poetry, law, and prophecy, written by numerous authors over several centuries. This anthology has profoundly influenced Western law, literature, and culture.

### [Abafi](https://elitereads.com/book/abafi-miklos-josika) by Miklós Jósika

Set in 16th-century Transylvania, this historical novel follows the moral transformation of a young nobleman from a life of hedonism to one of duty and self-discipline. ### [Researches into the Phenomena of Spiritualism](https://elitereads.com/book/researches-into-the-phenomena-of-spiritualism) by William Crookes

A collection of scientific reports documenting chemist William Crookes' experiments with mediums like Daniel Dunglas Home and Florence Cook in the 1870s. The text outlines his attempts to apply rigorous physical measurement to spiritualist phenomena such as levitation and materialization.

### [The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI](https://elitereads.com/book/the-worlds-i-see) by Fei-Fei Li

### [Slow Horses](https://elitereads.com/book/slow-horses-mick-herron) by Mick Herron

### [The Serviceberry: Abundance and Reciprocity in the Natural World](https://elitereads.com/book/the-serviceberry-abundance-and-reciprocity-in-the-natural-world) by Robin Wall Kimmerer

### [Co-Intelligence](https://elitereads.com/book/co-intelligence-living-and-working-with-ai) by Ethan Mollick

The text offers practical strategies for collaborating with smart machines while maintaining human identity.

### [Moby Dick](https://elitereads.com/book/moby-dick) by Herman Melville

The novel follows the sailor Ishmael and his voyage on the whaling ship Pequod, commanded by the obsessive Captain Ahab. ### [Inside the Tornado](https://elitereads.com/book/inside-the-tornado) by Geoffrey A. Moore

### [Autobiography of a Yogi](https://elitereads.com/book/autobiography-of-a-yogi) by Paramahansa Yogananda

### [1984](https://elitereads.com/book/1984) by George Orwell

The work examines how the manipulation of language and historical records can be used as tools of political oppression.

### [The Third Wave](https://elitereads.com/book/the-third-wave-steve-case) by Steve Case

### [The Reader](https://elitereads.com/book/the-reader) by Bernhard Schlink

### [Becoming](https://elitereads.com/book/becoming) by Michelle Obama

Michelle Obama's memoir chronicles her journey from her childhood on the South Side of Chicago to her tenure as First Lady of the United States. The book offers personal reflections on balancing motherhood and a professional career while navigating the pressures of life in the public eye.

### [Familiaris](https://elitereads.com/book/familiaris) by David Wroblewski

Set in 1919 Wisconsin, the story follows John and Mary Sawtelle as they build a farm and begin a multi-generational project to breed a unique line of extraordinary dogs. This expansive saga explores the profound bond between humans and animals alongside themes of friendship, legacy, and the pursuit of a purposeful life.

### [White Oleander](https://elitereads.com/book/white-oleander) by Janet Fitch

After her mother is imprisoned for murder, twelve-year-old Astrid Magnussen moves through a series of Los Angeles foster homes, each providing a distinct and often challenging environment. The story follows her journey from childhood to adulthood as she struggles with her mother's legacy and the search for her own identity. The novel explores themes of resilience, the complexity of maternal bonds, and the redemptive power of art.

### [The Good Earth](https://elitereads.com/book/the-good-earth) by Pearl S. Buck

Set in a rural Chinese village in the early 20th century, the novel follows the life of Wang Lung, a humble farmer whose devotion to the land brings him wealth and status. His journey from poverty to prosperity explores themes of family, tradition, and the cyclic nature of fortune amidst social and political upheaval.

### [A Guardian and a Thief](https://elitereads.com/book/a-guardian-and-a-thief) by Megha Majumdar

In a near-future Kolkata ravaged by extreme climate events and food scarcity, a woman's plans to join her husband in America are derailed when her family's immigration documents are stolen. The narrative alternates between the woman's frantic search and the perspective of the thief, exploring the moral compromises made in the name of family survival. This speculative thriller examines the collision of class, desperation, and hope in a city on the brink of collapse.

### [The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter](https://elitereads.com/book/the-heart-is-a-lonely-hunter) by Carson McCullers

Set in a small Georgia mill town during the 1930s, the novel follows a deaf-mute man named John Singer who becomes a confidant to various local misfits. Through their interactions, the story explores themes of spiritual isolation, racial tension, and the human search for understanding.

### [WKW: The Cinema of Wong Kar Wai](https://elitereads.com/book/wkw-the-cinema-of-wong-kar-wai) by Wong Kar Wai, John Powers

A comprehensive retrospective of the internationally acclaimed filmmaker Wong Kar Wai, presented through a series of conversations with critic John Powers. The volume explores his complete oeuvre across locations used in his most famous films, illustrated with over 250 photographs and film stills. It examines his signature themes of time, nostalgia, and beauty while detailing his unique approach to visual storytelling.

### [Snow Country](https://elitereads.com/book/snow-country) by Yasunari Kawabata

A tale of wasted love set in a remote hot spring town in the Japanese Alps. The story follows the doomed romance between a wealthy Tokyo dilettante and a provincial geisha against the backdrop of a stark, winter landscape.

### [Where I'm Calling From](https://elitereads.com/book/where-im-calling-from) by Raymond Carver

A definitive retrospective collection of short fiction compiled shortly before the author's death. The volume brings together thirty stories from previous collections with seven new works, documenting the evolution of Carver's influential minimalist style and his exploration of the struggles of ordinary working-class lives.

### [The Great Gatsby](https://elitereads.com/book/the-great-gatsby) by F. Scott Fitzgerald

Set in the Roaring Twenties on Long Island, the novel follows narrator Nick Carraway's encounters with the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby. Gatsby is obsessed with reuniting with his former lover, Daisy Buchanan, leading to a tragic exploration of social class and the disillusioned pursuit of the American Dream.

### [The Buenos Aires Affair](https://elitereads.com/book/the-buenos-aires-affair) by Manuel Puig

The novel follows the destructive intersection of two lives: Gladys, a sculptor tormented by sexual repression, and Leo, an art critic haunted by violent guilt. Set against the backdrop of political instability in mid-century Argentina, the narrative subverts the detective genre using experimental techniques like transcripts, notes, and cinematic references.

### [No Longer Human](https://elitereads.com/book/no-longer-human) by Osamu Dazai

A semi-autobiographical novel following the life of Yozo Oba, a man who feels profoundly alienated from society and adopts a clownish persona to hide his detachment. The narrative chronicles his descent into depression, alcoholism, and self-destruction in post-WWII Japan.

### [The Grapes of Wrath](https://elitereads.com/book/the-grapes-of-wrath) by John Steinbeck

The Joad family is forced from their Oklahoma farm during the Great Depression and Dust Bowl. They travel to California along Route 66 with thousands of other migrant workers, facing extreme hardship and social injustice.

### [Hopscotch](https://elitereads.com/book/hopscotch) by Julio Cortázar

A cornerstone of the Latin American Boom, this non-linear novel follows Horacio Oliveira, an Argentine intellectual navigating a bohemian life in Paris and Buenos Aires. The 'counter-novel' allows readers to follow multiple paths through its chapters, merging surrealist imagery with existential inquiry and jazz philosophy.

### [Norwegian Wood](https://elitereads.com/book/norwegian-wood) by Haruki Murakami

Set in late-1960s Tokyo, the novel follows college student Toru Watanabe as he navigates his relationships with two very different women. He is torn between the emotionally fragile Naoko and the vibrant, independent Midori while dealing with the grief of a shared past. The story explores themes of loss, sexuality, and the painful transition into adulthood.

### [Heartbreak Tango](https://elitereads.com/book/heartbreak-tango) by Manuel Puig

A multi-layered narrative of seduction and shattered dreams set in a small Argentine town during the 1930s and 40s. Using a style composed of letters, diary entries, and police reports, the novel parodies serial romances while exploring social hypocrisies and gender roles. The story centers on the lives of several women connected to a local charmer suffering from tuberculosis.

### [A Streetcar Named Desire](https://elitereads.com/book/a-streetcar-named-desire) by Tennessee Williams

Blanche DuBois, a fading Southern belle with a troubled past, moves into her sister Stella's cramped New Orleans apartment. Her arrival ignites a volatile conflict with Stella's brutish husband, Stanley Kowalski, leading to a tragic confrontation between illusion and reality.

### [Eight Million Ways to Die](https://elitereads.com/book/eight-million-ways-to-die) by Lawrence Block

Ex-cop and unlicensed private investigator Matthew Scudder attempts to find the killer of a young prostitute who sought his protection. Set in 1980s New York City, the novel explores the gritty reality of urban crime and Scudder's personal struggle with alcoholism.

### [The Stranger](https://elitereads.com/book/the-stranger) by Albert Camus

After the death of his mother, an emotionally detached man named Meursault commits a seemingly random murder on an Algerian beach. The narrative follows his trial and imprisonment, exploring the indifference of the universe and the philosophy of the absurd.

### [The Legend of the Condor Heroes](https://elitereads.com/book/the-legend-of-the-condor-heroes) by Jin Yong

Set in 13th-century China during the Song and Jin dynasties, this martial arts epic follows Guo Jing, a humble young man raised among Mongols under the protection of Genghis Khan. Guided by legendary kung fu masters, he must return to his homeland to face a predetermined duel amidst shifting political alliances and imperial warfare.

### [Blossoms](https://elitereads.com/book/blossoms) by Jin Yucheng

A sweeping portrait of Shanghai life following three childhood friends from the 1960s Cultural Revolution to the economic boom of the 1990s. The narrative captures the city's transformation and the complexities of human connection through a unique linguistic style influenced by the Shanghainese dialect.

### [The Physiology of Taste](https://elitereads.com/book/the-physiology-of-taste) by Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin

A fundamental work on gastronomy and the art of dining that established food as a subject of scientific and philosophical study. It explores the connection between the senses, culinary traditions, and human identity through anecdotes and meditations. The text is famous for the aphorism: 'Tell me what you eat, and I will tell you what you are.'

### [The Giving Tree](https://elitereads.com/book/the-giving-tree) by Shel Silverstein

A poignant picture book about the lifelong relationship between a boy and a selfless apple tree. As the boy grows and his demands increase, the tree provides everything it has, exploring themes of unconditional love and the nature of giving.

### [Way of the Warrior Kid](https://elitereads.com/book/way-of-the-warrior-kid) by Jocko Willink

After a difficult fifth-grade year marked by bullying and physical struggle, Marc spends his summer under the guidance of his Navy SEAL uncle. Through a structured regimen of exercise, martial arts, and disciplined study habits, he learns how to transform himself into a warrior.

### [World Order](https://elitereads.com/book/world-order) by Henry Kissinger

Henry Kissinger examines the history of global systems and the diverse concepts of order held by different civilizations. He analyzes the challenges of the twenty-first century, exploring how to build a shared international framework in a world of conflicting historical perspectives and proliferating technology.

### [Why Nations Fail](https://elitereads.com/book/why-nations-fail) by Daron Acemoglu, James A. Robinson

Acemoglu and Robinson argue that the economic success of nations depends on their political and economic institutions. They contrast 'inclusive' institutions, which encourage innovation and broad participation, with 'extractive' institutions designed to enrich a small elite. Using historical case studies, the book illustrates how these institutional paths determine long-term prosperity or poverty.

### [Ender's Game](https://elitereads.com/book/enders-game) by Orson Scott Card

In a future where humanity is threatened by an insectoid alien species, young Ender Wiggin is recruited into a rigorous orbital military academy. Through increasingly complex tactical simulations, Ender must prove his strategic genius to save Earth while navigating the psychological isolation and manipulation of his superiors.

### [On Immunity](https://elitereads.com/book/on-immunity) by Eula Biss

Eula Biss examines the history, science, and cultural myths surrounding vaccination through the lens of modern motherhood. The book explores metaphors of immunity and argues that health is a collective responsibility rather than an individual choice.

### [American Lion](https://elitereads.com/book/american-lion) by Jon Meacham

A detailed biography of Andrew Jackson's presidency, focusing on his personal life and inner circle in the White House. It examines how Jackson's complex character and controversial policies shaped the modern American presidency during a period of national upheaval.

### [The End of Power](https://elitereads.com/book/the-end-of-power) by Moisés Naím

An analysis of how the nature of power is transforming in the 21st century. The author argues that power is becoming easier to acquire but harder to use and easier to lose, shifting from large institutions to smaller, nimbler actors.

### [Decoded](https://elitereads.com/book/decoded-jay-z) by Jay-Z

### [The Muqaddimah](https://elitereads.com/book/the-muqaddimah) by Ibn Khaldun

A foundational work of historiography, sociology, and economics written in the 14th century by North African scholar Ibn Khaldun. It analyzes the cyclical nature of civilizations, the role of social cohesion known as 'asabiyyah', and the factors contributing to the rise and fall of political dynasties.

### [Dealing with China](https://elitereads.com/book/dealing-with-china) by Henry M. Paulson Jr.

Former U.S. Treasury Secretary Henry M. Paulson Jr. provides a behind-the-scenes account of China's rapid transformation into an economic superpower. Drawing on his experience as CEO of Goldman Sachs and a high-ranking statesman, he details his high-stakes negotiations with Chinese leaders like Xi Jinping. The book examines the evolution of state-controlled capitalism and offers insights into how Western leaders can navigate and engage with the Chinese system.

### [Open](https://elitereads.com/book/open-andre-agassi) by Andre Agassi

### [Orwell's Revenge](https://elitereads.com/book/orwells-revenge-peter-huber) by Peter Huber

### [The New Jim Crow](https://elitereads.com/book/the-new-jim-crow) by Michelle Alexander

### [Portfolios of the Poor](https://elitereads.com/book/portfolios-of-the-poor) by Daryl Collins, Jonathan Morduch, Stuart Rutherford, Orlanda Ruthven

This book examines the financial lives of people living on less than two dollars a day in Bangladesh, India, and South Africa. Using 'financial diaries' to track daily transactions, the authors demonstrate that poor households are active, sophisticated money managers who use informal tools to handle irregular incomes and financial risks.

### [The Last Days of Night](https://elitereads.com/book/the-last-days-of-night) by Graham Moore

### [The Structure of Scientific Revolutions](https://elitereads.com/book/the-structure-of-scientific-revolutions) by Thomas S. Kuhn

A foundational text in the philosophy of science that argues scientific progress occurs through episodic 'paradigm shifts' rather than steady accumulation. Kuhn describes how scientific communities work within established frameworks until anomalies precipitate a crisis, leading to a revolutionary change in perspective. This work introduced terms such as 'normal science' and 'incommensurability' into the academic lexicon.

### [The House of Rothschild](https://elitereads.com/book/the-house-of-rothschild-moneys-prophets-1798-1848) by Niall Ferguson

### [Gang Leader for a Day](https://elitereads.com/book/gang-leader-for-a-day) by Sudhir Venkatesh

### [The Dark Forest](https://elitereads.com/book/the-dark-forest) by Cixin Liu

### [The Aeneid](https://elitereads.com/book/the-aeneid) by Virgil

Commissioned by the emperor Augustus, this Latin epic poem follows Aeneas, a Trojan hero who travels to Italy and becomes the ancestor of the Romans. The narrative blends Greek myth with Roman history, exploring themes of fate, duty, and the foundation of a new civilization.

### [Physics of the Impossible](https://elitereads.com/book/physics-of-the-impossible) by Michio Kaku

Theoretical physicist Michio Kaku examines the scientific viability of technologies commonly found in science fiction, such as teleportation, time travel, and invisibility. He categorizes these concepts into three classes of 'impossibility' based on their relationship with the known laws of physics and evaluates when they might realistically be achieved.

### [Xi Jinping: The Governance of China](https://elitereads.com/book/xi-jinping-the-governance-of-china) by Xi Jinping

A compilation of 79 speeches, talks, and interviews delivered by Chinese President Xi Jinping between November 2012 and June 2014. The work provides an official overview of the leadership's philosophy, focusing on national rejuvenation, economic reform, and China's role in global governance.

### [The Varieties of Religious Experience](https://elitereads.com/book/the-varieties-of-religious-experience) by William James

A comprehensive study based on the 1901-1902 Gifford Lectures investigating individual religious experience as a psychological phenomenon. William James analyzes mysticism, conversion, and saintliness, applying a pragmatic approach to evaluate the functional truth of spiritual beliefs. The text remains a foundational work in both psychology and the philosophy of religion.

### [The Idea Factory](https://elitereads.com/book/the-idea-factory-jon-gertner) by Jon Gertner

### [The Information](https://elitereads.com/book/the-information-james-gleick) by James Gleick

### [Justice on Trial](https://elitereads.com/book/justice-on-trial) by Mollie Hemingway, Carrie Severino

The book examines the dysfunctional nature of the modern judicial confirmation process and the intense political drama surrounding high-stakes vacancies. It explores the future implications of these ideological battles for the nation's highest court.

### [The Prince](https://elitereads.com/book/the-prince) by Niccolò Machiavelli

A 16th-century political treatise providing an instructional guide for new princes on the acquisition and maintenance of political power. It is considered a foundational work of modern political philosophy, emphasizing pragmatism and realpolitik over traditional moral doctrines.

### [Rich Dad Poor Dad](https://elitereads.com/book/rich-dad-poor-dad) by Robert T. Kiyosaki, Sharon L. Lechter

The book explores the contrasting financial philosophies of the author's two fathers to illustrate principles of wealth building. It advocates for financial literacy, investing in assets, and entrepreneurship as the path to financial independence.

### [Ship of Fools](https://elitereads.com/book/ship-of-fools) by Tucker Carlson

Tucker Carlson examines the divergence between the American political elite and the general populace through the lens of Plato's ship of state allegory. He argues that leaders across the political spectrum have abandoned middle-class concerns in favor of identity politics and globalist economic policies.

### [All Quiet on the Western Front](https://elitereads.com/book/all-quiet-on-the-western-front) by Erich Maria Remarque

A semi-autobiographical account of the physical and mental stress German soldiers faced during World War I. The story follows Paul Bäumer, a young soldier whose idealistic views of patriotism are shattered by the brutal reality of trench warfare. It explores the 'lost generation' of men who were physically and psychologically destroyed by the conflict.

### [Exonerated](https://elitereads.com/book/exonerated-dan-bongino) by Dan Bongino

Former Secret Service agent Dan Bongino examines the investigations into the 2016 Trump campaign and the subsequent Mueller probe. The book analyzes how federal agencies and political actors utilized specific strategies to challenge the administration. Bongino details the origins of the Russiagate scandal and the motives behind the investigative efforts.

### [Trumponomics: Inside the America First Plan to Revive Our Economy](https://elitereads.com/book/trumponomics-inside-the-america-first-plan-to-revive-our-economy) by Stephen Moore, Arthur B. Laffer

Economists Stephen Moore and Arthur Laffer detail the economic framework of the Trump administration, focusing on tax reform, deregulation, and trade. Drawing from their experience as senior advisors, the authors provide an insider's perspective on the 'America First' agenda and its goals for national prosperity.

### [Unfreedom of the Press](https://elitereads.com/book/unfreedom-of-the-press) by Mark R. Levin

Levin examines how the modern American press has transitioned from a tradition of objective journalism to one of partisan advocacy and ideological uniformity. He explores the history of media from the Revolutionary-era patriot press to the rise of progressivism in the 20th century. The book argues that current threats to press freedom arise from internal factors like self-censorship and group-think rather than government suppression.

### [The Second World Wars](https://elitereads.com/book/the-second-world-wars) by Victor Davis Hanson

Victor Davis Hanson provides a thematic analysis of World War II, examining it as a single global conflict rather than a series of isolated regional wars. The book explores the strategic, economic, and industrial factors that led to the Allied victory and the defeat of the Axis powers across air, sea, and land.

### [Crippled America](https://elitereads.com/book/crippled-america-how-to-make-america-great-again) by Donald Trump

Donald Trump outlines his political agenda for the 2016 presidential election, detailing his positions on immigration, healthcare, the economy, and foreign policy. The book argues for a business-oriented approach to government reform based on his experience as a real estate developer.

### [The Fountainhead](https://elitereads.com/book/the-fountainhead) by Ayn Rand

Innovative architect Howard Roark refuses to compromise his unique creative vision for societal approval or professional success. The narrative follows his professional struggles and personal conflicts, illustrating the tension between individualism and collective conformity.

### [Midas Touch](https://elitereads.com/book/midas-touch-why-some-entrepreneurs-get-rich-and-why-most-dont) by Donald J. Trump, Robert T. Kiyosaki

Two business icons outline five essential traits for entrepreneurial success: strength of character, focus, brand, relationships, and attention to detail. The authors share personal anecdotes and lessons on financial literacy and resilience to illustrate how to build a global brand. The text contrasts the mindset of employees with that of entrepreneurs who turn challenges into opportunities.

### [Trump: Think Like a Billionaire](https://elitereads.com/book/trump-think-like-a-billionaire) by Donald J. Trump, Meredith McIver

Donald Trump shares strategies for developing a wealth-oriented mindset, focusing on real estate investment and professional career skills.
